items._cn_summary: 这是挪威 Camilla Hole Trio 的专辑《Langs》乐评。与前作融合科幻合成器音效的做法不同，这次专辑回归更'接地气'的方向，但仍延续对本国传统民间音乐的探索。主创 Camilla Hole 以高音萨克斯为核心乐器，爵士影响贯穿始终。乐评以开篇曲《Springleik》为例详细剖析：这首源自挪威西部民间舞蹈的曲子先由 Hole 奏出主旋律，贝斯手 Egil Kalman 与鼓手 Knut Kvifte Nesheim 提供节奏支撑，随后叠加 Kalman 的模块化合成器与 Nesheim 的颤音琴增添色彩。专辑的特色在于三位成员的角色界限模糊，Kalman 会在贝斯上接过旋律与 Hole 齐奏，Nesheim 则在节奏上不断拓展空间，整首作品逐渐走向自由即兴，Hole 在尾声再次奏出旋律收束。整体呈现出传统挪威民间音乐与爵士即兴、模块合成器音色相融合的独特面貌。

items.body: Review by alainPP — Green Carnation presents the third album in the "A Dark Poem" trilogy, nodding to the likes of Anathema and Katatonia. It delivers an oppressive, heavy, and meditative sound with dark progressive roots."Unconditional Artificial Chemistry" opens with a spacey feel, suddenly cut through by an exuberant, thick, heavy guitar; the monolithic vocals help transport the listener to another planet. The track narrates the dangers of AI, unfolding seamlessly while building an all-encompassing, progressive intensity. It shifts to include a crystalline piano in the distance, with musical grandeur that straddles the line between doom and Opeth-esque gothic metal, creating an oppressive atmosphere. There is a spellbinding melancholy'a blend of Anathema, Mogwai, Katatonia, and early King Crimson. "The Messiah Complex" features a melting guitar arpeggio, with vocals that abruptly break the ethereal, charming, and hypnotic mood. Melancholic, mysterious keyboards add a layer of solemnity that oozes progressive structure, while the dominant vocals allow the mantra-like atmosphere to spill over. The decrescendo finale is simple and effective'steady and unstoppable'serving as a musical paradigm."Broken Souls, Common Enemies" features a prominent New Wave-style synth driving the rhythm. The riff, the languid vocals, and the guitar's plaintive melody evoke emotion, discovery, and complexity in a track that is heavy without flaunting it. A shift to screamed vocals over a machine-gun riff'reminiscent of The Gathering in their early days'reasserts the track's intensity and complexity, bolstered by Wright-esque keyboards. A break featuring an ethereal flute and a melting, Western-style acoustic solo follows. Vocoded vocals amplify the majestic atmosphere, launching a stratospheric guitar solo worthy of the genre's titans'a truly stunning moment. Finally, "A Dark Poem - Orchestral Suite" begins with otherworldly vocals introducing wind instruments'including Ingrid's flute'as the orchestral arrangement takes center stage. An orchestral suite worthy of *Fantasia*'a classic pastoral anthem recounting Rimbaud's "Ophelia," performed by the Kristiansand Symphony Orchestra and its opera choir. Then comes the break: a return to archaic vocals, a primal sound reaching its zenith'is this the birth of prog? A dark, unsettling, yet colorful and pastoral atmosphere, pierced by illuminating trumpets; it is a masterpiece right up to the final note, with a soaring violin flourish creating a moment that transcends time.Green Carnation takes its final bow with this triptych finale'punchier, spellbinding, and invigorating. It is a crowning achievement, blending dystopian lyrics about our society with majestic, solemn melodies. Classy, ​​dreamlike, and immense progressive post-metal'featuring a sound that left an indelible mark on me from their very beginnings, delivering a powerful impact this September.
items._genre: experimental post-metal / progressive / gothic metal / orchestral
items._cn_summary: Green Carnation 推出"黑暗诗篇"三部曲终章，以阴郁、沉重且冥想式的实验前卫金属为核心，融合Anathema式的哀婉旋律与Opeth式的哥特金属质感。专辑曲目编排宏大，吉他音色厚重而具有雕塑感，键盘铺陈营造神秘庄严的氛围，歌词聚焦AI威胁等反乌托邦主题。终曲与挪威克里斯蒂安桑交响乐团及歌剧合唱团合作，以管弦乐组曲形式呈现兰波"奥菲利亚"的意象，融入长笛、小号与小提琴等古典元素，形成从重金属到管弦乐叙事的完整弧线。新浪潮合成器驱动、空灵长笛段落与原声吉他独奏的穿插，拓宽了金属乐的表现维度。整体展现出挪威乐队在金属与古典融合领域的成熟控制力，适合偏好前卫实验与跨界融合的听众。

items.body: Uboa releases the live album “Every Reactor Four a Friend (Live at Roadburn 2024)” through The Flenser on 22 September 2026, with a vinyl edition to follow as part of the label’s Membership Series 8 Exclusive. The three-track release is a recording of “Meltdown,” a piece Roadburn commissioned Uboa to compose for its 2024 edition. Uboa’s ‘Meltdown’ performance from Roadburn 2024 Roadburn commissioned Uboa to write two original works for its 2024 festival: “Calm Down,” a quieter piece, and its counterpart “Meltdown,” performed alongside TOomD’s “Shut Down.” “Every Reactor Four a Friend” is the live recording of “Meltdown,” captured from the mixing desk at Roadburn and later remixed and reworked, since some onboard vocal effects and microphones were missing from the available stems. The title refers to Reactor Four at Chernobyl, the reactor that melted down in the 1986 disaster. Musically, the release leans on power electronics and cut-up harsh noise, closer to the extremity of Uboa’s 2018 album “The Sky May Be” than the more intricate construction of her recent records. Uboa described the themes behind the performance directly: “It’s about embracing the overwhelm rather than shaming oneself for it. All the shame, anger and overwhelm was put in this short performance.” She added: “Sometimes it’s fine to just crash the fuck out. Sometimes it is necessary.” The album runs three tracks: “Dys,” “Do Not Comply In Advance” and “Ascension Threshold.” Every Reactor Four a Friend (Live at Roadburn 2024) by Uboa The Flenser also published a full-album stream of the performance: All Bandcamp proceeds from “Every Reactor Four a Friend” go toward covering Xandra’s gender-affirming surgery costs through 21 October 2026. About Uboa Uboa is a solo power electronics and noise project active since 2010, based in Melbourne, Australia. Early releases “Sometimes Light” (2010) and “Jouissance” (2013) were self-released before the 2018 album “The Sky May Be” arrived on the Australian label Art As Catharsis. “The Origin of My Depression” followed in 2019, initially self-released before The Flenser reissued it on vinyl after Uboa signed to the San Francisco label in February 2023. The Flenser then released the 2024 studio album “The Great Impossible Light,” featuring contributions from Blood of a Pomegranate, Otay:Onii, Charlie Looker and Haela Hunt-Hendrix of Liturgy. Uboa performed three sets at Roadburn Festival in Tilburg, Netherlands, in April 2024, including the live debut of “The Origin of My Depression” performed in full alongside the commissioned pieces “Calm Down” and “Meltdown.” “Every Reactor Four a Friend (Live at Roadburn 2024)” is the recording of that “Meltdown” performance, released through The Flenser two years on.
items._cn_summary: 这是Uboa于2024年在荷兰Roadburn音乐节演出现场录制的现场专辑，原作为受音乐节委约创作的作品《Meltdown》，后经混音台重新混制而成。标题灵感源自1986年切尔诺贝利核事故中熔毁的四号反应堆，主题围绕接纳情绪崩溃与过度刺激感，将愤怒、羞耻与失控感投射进表演之中。音乐以强力电子与切碎式噪音为核心，回归2018年专辑《The Sky May Be》时期的极端风格，曲目包括三段：《Dys》《Do Not Comply In Advance》《Ascension Threshold》。发行由The Flenser厂牌以黑胶与数字形式推出，数字版收益将用于帮助艺术家Xandra支付性别确认手术费用。文章内容偏向新闻发布性质，缺乏深度评论与分析。

items.body: I’ll always wait for you The promise that someone will wait forever has enjoyed an excellent reputation in love songs, considering how uncomfortable it can become outside them. Patience can deepen into devotion, but it can also give obsession an alibi, allowing someone to call an inability to let go proof of a superior kind of love. London trio Black Doldrums explore that uneasy territory on Waiting, a song whose tenderness comes with the unnerving suggestion that nobody has agreed on when the waiting should come to an end. The third single from Repetition Compulsion, due November 13th, 2026, via Fuzz Club, carries a particular connection to the band’s previous album. Written around the same time as In Limerence, it extends that record’s preoccupation with longing and romantic fixation into a love song that sounds both consoling and quietly bereft. Its accompanying video takes those feelings out into the city, where a solitary attachment becomes an increasingly threatening pursuit. A deep, humming bass and the heavy thud of drums establish the song’s measured pace, while a cool, jangling guitar melody moves between high, glassy notes and lower, mournful phrases. There is something of The Chameleons in the guitar’s arcing melodies, and of The Cure in the funereal weight beneath it. Sheets of icy synthesizer widen the space around the instruments, giving the opening a peculiar calm: everything sounds composed, even as the melody suggests that something has gone terribly wrong. When Kevin Gibbard begins singing, the synthesizers settle into warmer mid-range tones, bringing a little bodily comfort to that cold room. His voice carries some of Andrew Eldritch’s solemn authority in a slightly higher register, with an exposed ache that also recalls Ian Curtis. Beneath him, the guitar takes on an increasingly Cure-like character, its clear notes ringing against the low end. Then the chorus rises into “I’ll always wait for you,” stretching the promise into a lament. The guitar’s answering jangle supplies the small, involuntary chill, the sort that travels up an arm before the mind has decided whether the feeling is pleasure or dread. For all that unease, the song began in an ordinary moment of affection. Gibbard wrote the lyrics early one morning while waiting for Sophie Landers to wake up, with the themes of their second album still close at hand. “When we were going through the finished mixes of the second album, Sophie noticed this recurring theme of limerence, which pushed ‘Waiting’ further in that direction. I liked the idea of writing about waiting for someone you love, that if you love someone enough, you’ll wait forever. I wrote all the lyrics in one go, early one morning, while I was literally waiting for Sophie to wake up. I just started jotting it down.” Landers also supplied the idea behind one of the recording’s stranger details, asking for a sound that would suggest a spirit departing its body. Gibbard found his approximation through a Mellotron, voice synthesizers, and pitch bend: “Sophie wanted something that sounded like a soul leaving someone’s body. So I played around with a Mellotron and voice synths with pitch bend to create something similar. It seemed to fit nicely because it has this really haunting sound.” That imagined departure hangs over a song devoted to staying. The warmer synthesizers offer closeness, while the guitars and spectral vocal textures suggest distance, absence, and the possibility that a promise might outlast the person it was made to. There is considerable romance in Waiting, though very little reassurance that romance will make anyone happy. The video’s darker premise took shape during a recent viewing of Taxi Driver. Landers recognized connections between the film and the band’s interest in limerence, particularly its treatment of loneliness, idealization, mental distress, and destructive fixation. Black Doldrums developed those observations into a story about an isolated, obsessive man following a woman through the city, with his sense of control destined for a nasty correction. Gibbard and Landers occupy a nocturnal world of café booths, shuttered shopfronts, graffiti-covered brickwork, and stretches of nearly empty pavement. He sits alone with a cup, writes on a loose sheet of paper, and eats in a café; she walks through the streets in a black leather jacket, occasionally looking back. The editing brings their separate movements into an uncomfortable relationship, while red-lit close-ups of her eyes interrupt the greenish darkness outside. The ordinary business of getting through a night begins to feel charged with the possibility of being watched. As the distance between them closes, the action moves into a narrow pedestrian underpass, its fluorescent lights leaving little room for either figure to disappear. Landers walks ahead while Gibbard follows, until a look back changes the balance between pursuer and pursued. The closing image gives heartbreak an abruptly physical form, making the familiar business of giving someone your heart seem like an offer best considered carefully. Watch the video for Waiting below: Gibbard and Landers formed Black Doldrums in London, initially working as a duo built around guitar, drums, and vocals before expanding into a trio. Their 2022 debut Dead Awake and 2024 follow-up In Limerence, both released through Fuzz Club, brought their early interests in psychedelia, drone, and reverb into a more concentrated gothic post-punk form. Extensive UK and European touring followed, including arena dates supporting Archive and their own headline shows. Repetition Compulsion completes the band’s interconnected “State of Mind Trilogy,” exploring the emotional patterns people carry into relationships, memory, and self-understanding. Across eleven songs, the record expands those concerns into inherited behaviour, politics, and mental wellbeing. Waiting provides a particularly intimate connection between the trilogy’s final two chapters, holding affection and fixation close enough for their resemblance to become unsettling. The album arrives November 13th, 2026, on 180-gram neon-yellow vinyl limited to 350 hand-numbered copies, 180-gram ultra-clear vinyl, and CD. Pre-order the album here. Listen below and order via Bandcamp. items._cn_summary: 伦敦三人组合Black Doldrums的新单曲《Waiting》延续了前作《In Limerence》中对执念与浪漫迷思的主题探索。歌曲以深沉的嗡鸣贝斯线和厚重的鼓点奠定节奏基调，清亮的吉他旋律在高音区与低沉的哀悼性乐句之间游走，合成器音层拓展了空间感，营造出一种表面平静、内里不安的氛围。主唱Kevin Gibbard的声线带有庄严的权威感，裸露的痛感令人联想到Ian Curtis式的情感张力。副歌中'我会永远等你'的承诺被拉长成挽歌式的吟唱，吉他的回应带来不由自主的战栗。歌词诞生于等待爱人醒来的清晨一刻，将日常的温柔转化为关于痴迷与放手的哲学追问。

items.excerpt: 小気味良いホーンとパーカッションの響くファンキーなアフロビート“荊姫”での幕開けが、この2年ぶりのアルバムでの鮮やかなモード変化を物語る。ライヴ・バンドであるハハとヘアピンズの演奏を活かした楽曲が中心となり、月ノ美兎を迎えたメルヘン・ポップ“きたれりルート”やメロディアスなロック・ナンバー“蜜の主”があれば、松丸契のサックス・ソロをtofubeatsが実況中継するフリー（キー）ジャズ調のブレイクコア“ボス・モワレ・FS”や“我々不吉戦士”など構築美に溢れた音の快感もあり、曲の振り幅はいよいよ多彩。イメージを越えた地平でもっと素直に楽しまれていい傑作だ。

items._cn_summary: 長谷川白紙时隔两年推出的专辑以放克律动的非洲节拍开篇，展示了鲜明的模式转变。作品重心落在与现场乐队HaHa和Hairpins的合作上，既有邀请月ノ美兎参与的童话式流行曲，也有旋律感突出的摇滚曲目，更收录松丸契的萨克斯独奏与tofubeats实况解说交织的自由爵士式breakcore作品。整体在流行可听性与即兴结构之间反复游走，编曲层次丰富，曲目之间的风格跨度极为开阔，既有旋律直白的歌谣也有解构性的声音实验，体现出明确的构筑意识与跨界企图。

items.album: ExWHYZ『zION』80KIDZ、大沢伸一、パソコン音楽クラブらの高水準な楽曲を収めた名曲だらけのラストアルバム
items.tags: 邦楽 邦楽ポップ／ロック bounce 2026 September 邦楽 邦楽ポップ／ロック # アイドル 邦楽 ExWHYZ KBSNK ISLTR 80KIDZ 大沢伸一 パソコン音楽クラブ
items.excerpt: オリジナル・アルバムとしては3年ぶり3枚目、解散直前に届けた最後のアルバムは、高水準な楽曲をストイックに繰り出す美意識がとんでもない充実度で貫かれている。KBSNK＋ISLTRによる導入の“WHERE”が繊細な音世界にメランコリックな奥行きを提示したうえで、80KIDZや大沢伸一らによるソリッドなダンス・ビートが突き抜けるような享楽性を演出。そんななか、メンバー作詞の“SONNET”と“FADED”でエモい表情を覗かせるのもこの状況ならでは。終わらない空間の広がりを描いたパソコン音楽クラブ作の終曲“GIVE YOU MY WORD”が残す余韻も素晴らしい、名曲だらけの最高傑作だ。

items._cn_summary: ExWHYZ的告别专辑《zION》集合了80KIDZ、大沢伸一、パソコン音楽クラブ等不同创作者的作品，形成一张风格多元的电子拼盘。开场曲以KBSNK＋ISLTR的细腻音色营造忧郁氛围，随后转入硬朗的舞曲节拍，在纵欲感与内省之间反复切换。电脑音乐俱乐部操刀的终曲以延展的空间感收尾，余韵悠长。成员亲自填词的曲目展现出感伤的一面，与整体冷调美学形成呼应。作为乐队解散前的最后一作，专辑在情绪密度上有所提升，但评论侧重于情感氛围与制作水准的描述，未深入探讨声音设计的实验性或结构层面的突破。整体而言是一张完成度高、风格精致的电子专辑，适合偏好日式独立电子与氛围跨界制作的听众。

items.body: The Red Garland Quintet Featuring John Coltrane and Donald Byrd - Soul Junction (Prestige, 1960) Culinary writers frequently refer to comfort food. Soul Junction is my comfort music. I go to this album when I’m not in the mood to be blown away by wild flights of improvised fury or complex compositions or arrangements. This is an “end of an exhausting day” or a “reminder that maybe all will be well” kind of an album. I love the relaxed, bluesy feel of it. Listen to Garland’s piano on the opening title track. It’s pure bliss. George Joyner’s bass is understated perfection. The piano trio portion of the track goes on so long and is so hypnotic that you’re to be forgiven if you forget there’s a sax and trumpet still to come. Hey, there’s the saxophone. It feels like Trane was digging Garland’s playing and was dying to join in. Recorded in 1957, Trane hadn’t perfected his style yet. But his genius is right there to hear. He’s fantastic on Dizzy’s classic Birk’s Works . Donald Byrd doesn’t get much mention on this website, but I love a lot of his Blue Note music. He’s the perfect trumpeter for this session. Garland wisely gives the two of them lots of space to play, and they take every advantage of it. John Coltrane- First Meditations (For Quartet) ( Impulse!, 1977) As far as I’m concerned, A Love Supreme is the greatest jazz album of all time and Coltrane’s classic quartet the greatest group. First Meditations (For Quartet) is a beautiful piece of music and a fascinating document of a band just on the verge of transforming, both in terms of its personnel and its approach to music. (I prefer to say “transforming” to “ending”.) The first track, Love, clearly recalls A Love Supreme, as if that classic album is the starting point of this new music. Trane is stunning as always and McCoy is the perfect accompanist. The best track, Joy, is relatively calm and peaceful, until it isn’t. It begins as any number of other tracks from this quartet and then Trane sits out. He’s let the remaining trio play some (for this group) fairly straightforward piano trio music. But then he returns with an absolute roar, as if he wants to break constraints the rest of us can’t see. This is one of several places you can see the seams of the band starting to tear. It’s fascinating to hear. Much of this music was reconsidered on the subsequent album Meditations with Trane’s new group. A comparison of the two albums and the approach of two different groups to the material is fascinating, the second album justifiably being the more renowned of the two. But I find the first to be the one I keep returning to, as if I don’t want to say goodbye to this quartet. I genuinely love this album, but I had an ulterior motive for writing about it here. It gives me the opportunity to tell the story of the time I met Elvin Jones. He had been doing a drum demonstration and a line formed afterwards for autograph seekers. When I arrived at the front of the line, I barely refrained from doing “We’re not worthy”, but I did tell him how much his music meant to me and said I’d be honored if he’d sign this album. He took the CD booklet from me, looked at it and asked “Did I play on this?”. (I assume that since the album wasn’t released until 10 years after it was recorded, he never saw the album cover.) I showed him his name in the booklet, he laughed and signed it, making this album all the more special to me. Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评涵盖两张专辑。《Soul Junction》是Red Garland五重奏1957年的录音，氛围放松蓝调化，钢琴三重奏段落催眠般绵长，Coltrane在此尚未形成成熟个人风格但天赋已显露，Donald Byrd的小号恰到好处。《First Meditations (For Quartet)》则是经典四重奏向新方向转变的过渡记录，开篇Love回溯《A Love Supreme》，Joy一曲中Coltrane在平静段落后的爆发展示了乐队即将撕裂的接缝，与后续加扩充乐队的Meditations形成对照。评论语言个人化、带有强烈情感投射，结尾还穿插了作者与Elvin Jones相遇的轶事，但文末似乎被截断。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是低音单簧管演奏家安德鲁·德安杰洛的首张个人作品，整张唱片从头到尾只使用低音单簧管一件乐器，探索这一木管乐器的极限表现力。乐评指出低音单簧管是一种奇妙而独特的乐器，而此作彻底打消了任何对其作为世界最伟大木管的疑虑。德安杰洛本人是多乐器演奏家，但在此选择以单一乐器的纯粹形式呈现，专注于声音的可能性与即兴延展。专辑由小厂牌Loveland发行，属于先锋爵士与实验音乐范畴，对于关注自由即兴和前卫木管演奏的听众而言是一次集中的音色实验。原文为节选片段，信息有限，但已传达出专辑的核心方向——以低音单簧管为中心的自由探索与声响拓展。

items._cn_summary: 本文介绍了Burning Ambulance杂志对韩国裔美国作曲家及古筝类乐器komungo演奏者Jin Hi Kim的九碟套装选辑的评论。评论聚焦其中五张录音作品，涵盖其管弦乐与室内乐创作，以及与Susie Ibarra、Derek Bailey、Tony Oxley、Oliver Lake和William Parker等即兴音乐家的合作演奏。全套共52首曲目，横跨作曲与即兴两大领域，呈现了一位亚裔艺术家在西方当代音乐与亚洲传统乐器之间寻求交汇的创作轨迹。komungo作为韩国传统弦乐器，与自由爵士及先锋即兴语境的碰撞是该选辑的核心看点，体现出传统亚洲器乐在非西方古典语境下的实验性拓展。原文为转引式的乐评摘录，内容较短，缺少具体的音乐细节与个人聆听评价。

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦于瑞典Supertraditional音乐节，展现欧洲实验性民间音乐场景的跨界图景。作者Patrick Clarke从法国前卫民谣双人组La Tène和Sourdure的现场出发，串联起瑞典、西班牙、英格兰利兹等地的音乐人，涵盖电子风笛、利兹实验民谣等跨地域声响。文章同时推荐了十张关键新专辑，呈现传统乐器与电子手段、实验手法相融合的多元面貌。音乐节作为平台让不同国家的音乐人相互交流，推动了实验民谣这一小众领域的发展。整体而言，乐评关注的是传统音乐被解构与重组的过程，涉及民俗素材与现代表达的结合，但作为一篇专栏导览式的预告文章，实际唱片细节和深度评论相对有限。

items.body: Merryn Jeann Fear Of The Beauty Parlour Australian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist finds tenderness in fragments on her second album At what point does a song stop being a song? Strip away the beat, harmony and narrative; leave behind a voice, a melody, a few repeated words, the hiss of a phone recording. Merryn Jeann’s Fear Of The Beauty Parlour seems fascinated by precisely that threshold. Jeann has never been particularly interested in conventional singer-songwriting. In the Australian artist’s music, the voice can transform into an instrument, a simple melody can suddenly break off, and an intimate story can give way to a field recording, a strange synth sound or a seemingly random noise. On Dog Beach, producer Rob Ellis helped her organise these eccentric... The post Merryn Jeann – Fear Of The Beauty Parlour appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 澳大利亚创作人兼多乐器演奏者Merryn Jeann的第二张专辑聚焦于"歌曲何时不再是歌曲"这一临界地带。她将人声转化为纯粹乐器，旋律在途中断裂，私人叙事让位于田野录音、陌生合成器声响与随机噪音。制作人Rob Ellis协助她在前作Dog Beach的基础上梳理这些碎片化的即兴元素。有趣的是，The Quietus将本专辑归入审美对话阵营，与海象即兴三部曲形成隐性联动。专辑将民谣骨架包裹在实验外衣中，录音质感保留粗粝原始的状态，气息作为乐器与合成器形成美学对话。这是一张为爱好者准备的作品，在熟悉之上叠加陌生感。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Justin Greaves' band, Crippled Black Phoenix, embarks on a conceptual work exploring historically discriminated minorities, alongside themes of animal metaphors, massive blackouts, and social chaos. Setting such a scenario to music warranted a double album; from the opening track, "Incantation for the Different," one gets the impression of witnessing the workings of a secret order, sacrifices and rituals, where nothing is left to chance and every action carries a deliberate consequence. A dark, guttural, almost shamanic chant gives way to an atmosphere reminiscent of Portishead, the band led by Geoff Barrow, who produced and mentored them in their early days.Wyches and Basterdz is progressive yet dark, reminiscent of Nick Cave & The Bad Seeds during their more baroque phase; there is an otherworldly, epic quality to it, along with a rhythmic, psychedelic pulse that envelops the listener. This atmosphere is created by the perfect balance of Andy Taylor's baritone guitar, Helen Stanley's synthesizers, and, above all, Belinda Kordic's vocals.A distorted foundation serves as a backdrop; once the curtain parts, a choir enters, reminiscent of a secret gathering in Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut, yet here transporting us to the 15th and 17th centuries and the era of witch hunts. The choir makes a stealthy entrance and steadily gains ground; indeed, the title "Banefyre" is a play on "bonfire", the pyres where the accused were burned.Curiously, that pervasive, oppressive, and ominous atmosphere does not dampen the album's spirit; nor does it ever feel hollow, as there are classical echoes and dark elements, blending, as it were, the darkest side of The Cure with The Who, alongside Celtic influences in "The Reckoning" and a punk energy. Others, like Bonefire, are a bit more predictable, breaking the spell, though not the mood."Rose of Jericho" creates an atmosphere, amidst the contrasting guitar and trumpet, reminiscent of a blend between King Crimson and The Polyphonic Spree; it is sung by the other guitarist, Joel Segerstedt, and stands as just the first of the album's lengthy tracks. Disc two features "Down the Rabbit Hole," marking the return of Belinda Kordic, the band's answer to Beth Gibbons and Sonja Kristina. Here, with a blend of restrained tension and a certain raw texture alongside dreamlike moods that induce a trance-like state within a dissonant, psychedelic twilight, the sudden acceleration and the chorus act as lit candles bringing a touch of civilization.Everything Is Beautiful But Us speaks all too eloquently of the human place within the human ecosystem, judging by our actions over the last few centuries, without even factoring in the use of reason, which gives rise to self-awareness."The Pilgrim" brings a bit more sonic variety, once again featuring an interplay between guitar and synthesizers, and it all seems to have been a lead-up to "The Scene is a False Prophet," a warm-up and atmospheric build-up for that fifteen-minute suite. It is a journey through a seemingly endless tunnel, an experience that truly must be lived through, and the result is as rewarding as it is radical. It leaves behind echoes that reverberate and hum long after the music stops. The power of those three guitars, driving what is clearly the album's centerpiece, is undeniable, both in performance and composition. Like a bonfire built with quality logs, the fire and its light endure all night, radiating the warmth of that rift opened in time.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / dark folk / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这张双专辑以历史上受迫害的少数群体为概念核心，围绕动物隐喻、社会混沌等主题构建叙事。开场曲以低沉的萨满式吟唱营造秘密结社般的仪式感，随后展开融合巴洛克元素与凯尔特影响的暗色调乐章。贝琳达·科迪奇的人声被比作贝丝·吉本斯与索尼娅·克里斯蒂娜的结合，在合成器与失真吉他的张力间穿行。安迪·泰勒的低音吉他和海伦·斯坦利的合成器构成音乐骨架，而合唱团的隐秘介入呼应着十五至十七世纪猎巫运动的残酷历史。专辑中段混入朋克冲劲与古典回声，既保持了整体阴郁氛围又不显空洞。部分曲目如《Bonefire》较为可预测，略显打破了作品的催眠感。整体而言，这是一张概念完整、氛围层次丰富的概念专辑。

items.body: Review by Rysiek P. — An opportunity like this certainly cannot be overlooked. Twenty years after releasing their debut album, *Armed Forces of Simantipak*, the band Khatsaturjan?whose name derives from the renowned Armenian composer Aram Khachaturian?has released a new record titled *Monolog Chronosa*. Their discography also includes two other albums - *Disconcerto Grosso* (2010) and *Beast, Machine & Man* (2015) - and their history is notable for the fact that, as early as their 2002 debut single *Aramsome Sums*, they performed their own "rock" versions of Modest Mussorgsky's *Night on Bald Mountain* and Hector Berlioz's *March to the Scaffold*. All of this was presented in progressive hard-rock arrangements that incorporated elements reminiscent of the band Gentle Giant. Furthermore, critics hailed the group's first album as a benchmark for symphonic rock. One might pessimistically remark, "But that was years ago". Yet, it is certainly worth checking out where Khatsaturjan stands today. The band's latest release comprises forty-seven minutes of music spread across seven tracks, with an album title suggesting that the passage of time is the central theme. This phenomenon is observed and described from various perspectives - including, perhaps most importantly, the human condition and the personal, often highly subjective experience of life passing by. The title of the opening track - "Lessons (On Human Obsolescence)" - gives one food for thought right from the start. However, do not expect dark, atmospheric arrangements here. The composition is remarkably balanced,almost conservative in its playing style and employs familiar progressive rock tropes, with one notable exception: a strong emphasis on vocal polyphony (a true hallmark of this album) and a more prominent role for keyboards. These two elements define the musical structure of the song, which opens with the sound of a bell before embarking on a progressive journey rich in engaging tempo shifts and instrumental virtuosity. The second track, "What Was True," takes a slightly different approach. Here, the band clearly leans toward a modern progressive sound, successfully utilizing "new textures" to craft a unique atmosphere that straddles the line between atmospheric progressive rock (or even neo-prog) and a vocal-harmony-driven ballad. Once again, vocal polyphony and synthesizers serve as the building blocks for both this specific track and the album as a whole. The track "The Dystopian Spirit Of Club Energy" also features a piano-and-synthesizer-driven sound. Yet, in this composition, the band draws upon classical music and classical time signatures. The piano sets the arrangement's course, serving as a backdrop for highly impressive vocal performances. Only halfway through does the track remind us that it is 2026, showing how a guitar-driven rhythmic boost can yield a truly successful result. Incorporating electronic elements into the arrangement only enhances the musical value of this piece, which runs over five minutes in length. It was only while listening to "Song Of Days" that I realized what truly draws me to the band's music: a delicacy and almost theatrical storytelling style, skillfully blended with classical influences, alongside magnificent tales sung with a masterful, gradual build-up of vocal intensity. With a full arsenal of musical tools at their disposal, Khatsaturjan selects only those that fit the symphonic-progressive narrative, all while keeping classical music traditions close at hand. "Song Of Days" is a perfect example of this approach. It makes brilliant use of symphonic arrangements, blending them with flawless vocal lines and weaving in thoroughly modern progressive guitar motifs to create a truly well-crafted track. "DID Memoir" shares a similar, song-oriented character. It opens with a "classic" sense of grandeur, progressive guitar work, and... such delicate vocals. Everything weaves together into a structure that challenges the listener - filled with improvisational passages that hark back to classical music and, as an added bonus, theatrical farce-style interludes appearing midway through the fourth minute. Just listen closely around the five-minute mark for a dose of rap; this element, yet another instance of the piece's stylistic multiplicity, is entirely justified given the title: "DID Memoir." While the acronym refers to Dissociative Identity Disorder, it also serves as a fitting title for the track's eclectic, multi-stylistic nature. Following a symphonic opening, the penultimate track on this magnificent album - "The Keepers of the Philosopher's Stone" - simply sends shivers down the spine with its superb vocal lines. It features backing vocals, humming passages, and a lead vocal that stands out tonally, its rough timbre lending an air of deep mystery. Yet, what makes this composition truly exceptional is the extensive and successful incorporation of motifs drawn from classical music; the violin sounds and classical time signatures transform this five-plus-minute piece into a remarkable puzzle of motifs and an intricate arrangement. A madrigal-like character, blended with thoroughly modern synthesizer and guitar sounds, seems to elevate the track's central theme - fittingly so for a song about the "Philosopher's Stone," which here truly transmutes individual notes into "gold." With this release, the end comes all too soon. Were it not for the fact that the closing track - "Mundus Meus (This World of Mine)" - employs every possible device to captivate the listener from the very first note, one might feel that the magnificent preceding track left something musically unresolved, a void that could neither be filled nor replaced. "Mundus Meus..." stands as a magnificent anthem and the perfect culmination of the album; the Latin lyrics sound both prophetic and majestic without detracting from the depth of the message. And although the track features numerous gentle prog-metal solos, it remains, at its core, a thoroughly symphonic-progressive composition. If I say that I am very - truly very - pleasantly surprised by the latest work from the group Khatsaturjan, is that recommendation enough? If not, I'll add that the band features essentially the same lineup as on their debut and subsequent albums, even though musical light-years have passed since that first release (in 2002). Atte Kurri (vocals, bass, keyboards), Ilkka Piispala (vocals, drums, keyboards, bass), and Ilkka Saarikivi (vocals, keyboards, bass, violin) continue to demonstrate that musical trends don't matter to them. It is significant that Khatsaturjan is a group of friends who get together only when they want to record something; they are not a band that makes a living from touring and recording albums. On their Facebook page, the band writes: "We work slowly because Khatsaturjan is not our profession - it is a passion project and a beloved hobby. Whenever we decide to work on a new album, we know a years-long effort lies ahead, with no financial reward whatsoever. Yet, time and again, we take on new projects." Perhaps this approach allows them to maintain a sense of detachment and find the tranquility needed to create new music? You surely know that things tend to flow more easily when there are no deadlines hanging over your head. And since we will likely have to wait a long time for the next sign of musical life from Khatsaturjan, we should simply enjoy this highly successful release - one that has earned a spot in my top ten albums of the year.
items._genre: symphonic prog / progressive rock / vocal polyphony / neo-prog
items._cn_summary: 亚美尼亚乐队Khatsaturjan时隔多年发行新作《Monologue of Chronos》，专辑以四十七分钟七首曲目探讨时间流逝与人类境衰的主题。乐评指出乐队延续了早期对古典作品进行摇滚改编的传统，音乐风格被描述为'保守'的前卫摇滚，融合了交响化编排与人声复调这两个核心元素。键盘与合成器在作品中占据突出地位，开场曲以钟声起始并展开丰富的节奏变化与器乐炫技。第二首曲目偏向现代前卫摇滚与新前卫风格，利用新质感营造氛围。另一曲目以钢琴与合成器驱动，借鉴古典音乐与古典拍号，仅在中段加入吉他驱动的节奏推动力。整体而言，评论描述这是一张技法扎实、以人声复调为标志的前卫摇滚专辑，但更偏向传统谱系内的演变而非突破性实验。

items.album: Sandie Trash announces ‘Poupée Panik’, featuring Eric Debris and Richard Belgium
items.excerpt: Sandie Trash announces the single “Poupée Panik,” featuring Eric Debris (Métal Urbain) and Richard Belgium (MI6), the first track revealed from the upcoming album “Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka.” The French post-punk and new wave project has not confirmed a release date for the album itself, and “Poupée Panik” is not yet available on Sandie Trash’s Bandcamp page, Instagram or Facebook. Sandie Trash builds ‘Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka’
items.body: Sandie Trash announces the single “Poupée Panik,” featuring Eric Debris (Métal Urbain) and Richard Belgium (MI6), the first track revealed from the upcoming album “Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka.” The French post-punk and new wave project has not confirmed a release date for the album itself, and “Poupée Panik” is not yet available on Sandie Trash’s Bandcamp page, Instagram or Facebook. Sandie Trash builds ‘Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka’ around the Motel Dakota The nine-track album is set around a recurring fictional location, Room 17 of the Motel Dakota, with several tracks written as character pieces tied to that setting: “La perversita,” “Poupée Panik,” “Élégance déplacée,” “Gloria Dakota” and “Sophie qui aime les avions.” Sandie Trash describes the record as a “sabotage” of eighties nostalgia rather than a nostalgic homage to the decade. Alongside Eric Debris and Richard Belgium, the album credits a wide cast of guest contributors: Emmanuelle 5 (Dead Sexy), Olivier de Joie (Les Fils de Joie), Max Freeth (Ausgang), Karbokroma, Kelsey Warren (Blak Emoji), Jérôme Lefdup (Lefdup & Lefdup), Gilles Le Guen (Denner) and Oli Le Baron (Ici Paris). One track, “I Trash You Fuck Off,” is credited with a guest vocal from Helno, the former Lucrate Milk member who went on to front Les Négresses Vertes until his death in January 1993. Sandie Trash’s announcement does not explain how that vocal appears on a track dated 2026, whether as a sample, an archival recording or another arrangement, and no further detail was available to confirm it. Eric Debris also mixed and mastered the album at ATX Mastering studio. The cover art is by Italian illustrator Volt.B. About Sandie Trash Sandie Trash is a French punk and electro project based in Périgueux, fronted by the singer of the same name and built, album after album, around a rotating cast of guest musicians on individual tracks. The approach dates back at least to 2018, when the project’s “Le French Peep Show” paired a new musician with each song on the record. On Bandcamp, Sandie Trash’s confirmed discography includes the album “Outrageous brune,” released 25 February 2010 through Indies.Music.Productions with vocals from Sandie Trash and Maudd and mixing and mastering by Emmanuel Borie, and the 14-track compilation “Rose chewing-gun & Machine-gum (2006-2017),” released 29 May 2025 and gathering tracks and features from that decade, including contributions from Kloot Per W, Romeo Praly, Kim Ohio Fuzz, Marcel Vanthilt and Nina Courson. “Poupée Panik” and the album built around it, “Jeunes filles mödernes & Bazooka,” continue that same collaborative format on a larger scale, bringing in musicians tied to Métal Urbain, MI6, Ausgang, Denner and other underground post-punk and EBM circles for a post-punk and new wave record set inside the fictional Motel Dakota.
items._cn_summary: Sandie Trash 是来自法国佩里格尔的朋克与电子计划，围绕 Motel Dakota 17 号房这一虚构场景构建九首曲目式的概念专辑，多首作品以角色叙事方式创作。专辑邀请大量客座乐手参与，包括来自 Métal Urbain 的 Eric Debris、MI6 的 Richard Belgium，以及 Ausgang、Denner、Les Négresses Vertes 等地下圈子的音乐人。已故的 Helno 也在其中一首作品中贡献了客席人声，文章指出其录音来源（采样、档案录音或其他安排）未获说明。Eric Debris 负责整张专辑的混音与母带处理。创作者将这张作品定位为对八十年代怀旧情绪的破坏性介入，而非致敬性回顾。整体延续了项目自 2018 年以来每曲搭配不同合作者的传统框架，合作规模在此进一步扩大。

items.body: As you are likely well aware, this week marks the 100th anniversary of John Coltrane's birth and writers and friends of the Free Jazz Blog were asked to contribute their personal thoughts on his music and influence. The parameters for the contributions were loose, only that it should be something personal and if it so happened that an album appeared more than once, that was fine, as what it meant to the writer was surely different. We ended up with our biggest feature ever! For the next two weeks we will be featuring reflections, reviews, and anecdotes about Coltrane and his groundbreaking music. We begin today an introduction from Sammy Stein. Enjoy! Paul Acquaro John Coltrane. Src: wikipedia By Sammy Stein FJC is celebrating John Coltrane’s 100 th year. For anyone unfamiliar with his music, the following offers a brief overview of why Coltrane is ranked amongst the greatest of musicians. Through his approach, style, delivery, and unmistakable sound, Coltrane powered through the door that Ornette Coleman and others had left ajar, revealing jazz’s powerful, emotive, and transformational heart. Nothing post-Coltrane is untouched by his influence. His was not a deliberate subversion of traditional jazz, but an uncalculated stream of events, personal, spiritual, and historical, that converged in a confluence that formed his music. Coltrane’s mother bought him a saxophone when he was sixteen, and he was influenced by players including Illinois Jacquet. His grandparents were ordained ministers, his parents met through the church, and Coltrane grew up influenced by religion. He chose a different path – that of music and was not discouraged by family, yet later in his life, it was God who helped him save his music and career. Without his spiritual reawakening, Coltrane’s career may have faded. Early on, he was supported by musicians who recognised his prodigious talent. However, he became addicted to drugs and would arrive for gigs unshaven and in smelly, wrinkled clothes. He might fall asleep on stage. Miles Davis fired him, and Dizzy Gillespie didn’t follow suit only because of their friendship and his respect for Coltrane’s talent. At the nadir of his life, Coltrane reached out to God. He described a revelation he had when God spoke to him, and he set about composing exquisite music, praising God and teaching his followers. He said, “My goal is to live the truly religious life and express it through my music. If you can live it, there’s no problem about the music, because it’s part of the whole thing.” Coltrane’s first wife, Naima, was central to his early spiritual journey. A practicing Muslim, she helped him understand God’s presence in their lives. With her support, he overcame addiction within a year. His second wife, Alice, became his spiritual partner and musical collaborator. A pianist and harpist, she understood Coltrane’s desire to contribute to a greater purpose through music. Some of Coltrane’s music has an intangible quality. He understood the spiritual and temporal worlds, and his music fused the two, expressing deep spiritual inquiry alongside the mortal complexities of personality. Jazz became a place where the human condition could be expressed with unflinching honesty and transcendent beauty. Coltrane was playing at a time when conditions were ripe for rebellion and change, and he was profoundly affected by events of his time, especially the civil rights movement, initially siding with Malcolm X before aligning with Martin Luther King Jr’s belief in peaceful but persistent protest. He performed eight benefit concerts to support Martin Luther King Jr’s cause. His music channeled anger at racism and discrimination, despair at humanity’s darkness, and the beauty of praise and worship. He had faced the demons of addiction and won, and his music reflected beauty, was personal yet spoke to millions. The murder of four African American girls in the KKK bombing in Birmingham, Alabama, in 1963 profoundly affected Coltrane. Two months after the event, he took McCoy Tyner, Jimmy Garrison, and Elvin Jones into Rudy Van Gelder's studio and recorded ‘Alabama’, later released on the album Live At Birdland (Impulse 1964). As discontent rose, Coltrane’s modal technique challenged preconceived ideas about traditional jazz. Under his and other musicians’ tenure, jazz, ever the mirror of society, became more dissonant and unruly. Coltrane’s music is as relevant today as it was in the 1960s. The messages are clearly and profoundly expressed and cut to the core impulses of humanity. Because of his uncloaked humanity, listening to Coltrane feels as emergent and alive for someone encountering the music today as it did to listeners forty years, or ten years ago. Coltrane’s near-mythical status was helped by the Blue Note label, which signed Coltrane and other players, seen as risky at the time, and some iconic images, notably photographs by Francis Wolff, a skilled photographer and executive of Blue Note. Of over 33,000 pictures Wolff took (probably more), his images of John Coltrane in moments of intense concentration or creativity seem to capture the musician's essence. One of Coltrane’s gifts was his ability to perform as a soloist or as part of an ensemble. Pieces like Davis’s’ ‘Milestones’ with ‘Cannonball’ Adderley (alto sax) and Coltrane (tenor sax) responding to Davis’s trumpet with twists and turns within the original mode laid a template for modal playing (try also Coltrane's’ Spiral’ and ‘Naima’ from Giant Steps (Atlantic 1959)). Modal jazz led away from traditional jazz and toward free jazz. Free playing was where Coltrane was headed. In the 1960s, some journalists described early free jazz as a poison to jazz, and Downbeat critics described Coltrane and Dolphy’s playing as ‘nihilistic exercises’ and ‘anti-jazz.’ Miles Davis found free jazz difficult to embrace initially. However, a few years later Davis, like Coltrane and others, found free jazz liberating. Coltrane, like many free-playing musicians, connected the evolution of the music with a deepening of self-realization and the strengthening and expression of their beliefs. Alongside fellow musicians Yusef Lateef, Sonny Rollins, and others, Coltrane pursued musical mastery and self-realization. In his suite A Love Supreme (Impulse, 1965), Coltrane expressed his love and awe of God, and the final movement is based on a devotional poem he wrote. He studied different religions and philosophies, including the Indian philosophy of Jiddu Krishnamurti, which he was introduced to by Bill Evans. Coltrane perhaps expressed his love for God most during his free playing. His tracks ‘Love’ and ‘The Father, And The Son And the Holy Ghost’ on Meditations (Impulse 1965), albums Ascension (Impulse 1966), Om (Impulse, recorded 1965, released 1966), and ‘Peace on Earth’ from Infinity (Impulse, recorded 1966, released 1972), reflect his beliefs. Coltrane used the ferocity of his playing and complex techniques as a way of worship. He said he created music for God and others and wanted to be the opposing force to evil. Even those unaware of his driving beliefs find something special, untouchable, and unique in his music. Coltrane, Art Blakey, Yusef Lateef, and other musicians became part of the Ahmadiyya sect of Islam, which forbids the intake of drugs and alcohol. Coltrane said, "My music is the spiritual expression of what I am - my faith, my knowledge, my being. When you begin to see the possibilities of music, you desire to do something really good for people, to help humanity free itself from its hang-ups…I want to speak to their souls.” Some found Coltrane’s later music, with its contradictions and unresolved transitions, less pure than his earlier recordings, but for many, they remain some of the best work produced by any jazz musician. Two weeks before his death, Coltrane discussed opening a music venue without alcohol as he realized this had masked his creativity. After Coltrane died in 1967, aged just forty, Alice kept pushing musical boundaries, and her music took on a profoundly spiritual element. She collaborated with Ornette Coleman, Pharoah Sanders, and many others, and her music traversed from blues-infused melodies to unfathomable sonic journeys, but it was beautiful, and her talent won armies of devotees, so, partly through Alice, Coltrane’s legacy remained. Also through his sons. John Jr, Ravi, and Oranyan. Oranyan started playing jazz with his brothers but has gone into trance and electronic music production. John Jr was a promising bassist but was killed in a car accident when he was 17, and Ravi is a jazz musician. Alice’s grandnephew, Steven Ellison, AKA Flying Lotus, is a record label owner, producer, rapper, and DJ. Many of his recordings feature jazz samples. Coltrane’s music and persona continue to influence music and musicians. From those who followed directly, including Pharoah Sanders, Lonnie Liston, Sun Ra, Don Cherry, and John McLaughlin, to nearly every jazz musician today. In 2016,’ Alabama’ was included in John DeJohnette's 2016 album In Movement (ECM), and on this recording, sons of the original artists, including saxophonist Ravi Coltrane (son of Coltrane) and bassist Matthew Garrison (son of bassist Jimmy Garrison), played. Coltrane’s music has been sampled on recordings by hip hop artists, younger jazz musicians, and many others. FJC is celebrating the fact that Coltrane left his influence, and there are some great pieces following this introduction. It is impossible to adequately record the influence of John Coltrane on the music that followed, but we can try. As a jazz musician recently said to me, ‘Don’t worry, just stick on some ‘Trane.” Perhaps more than any other jazz musician, John Coltrane showed there is a way to play from the heart without constraints. When you can do that, you allow your true spirit to reveal itself. Like ‘Trane. Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook

items._cn_summary: 本文是Free Jazz Blog为纪念John Coltrane诞辰100周年而策划的大型专题导言，由Sammy Stein撰写。文章并非针对单一专辑的深度乐评，而是以个人化叙述方式梳理了Coltrane的音乐生涯与精神轨迹：从早年因毒瘾被Miles Davis解雇的谷底，到宗教觉醒后重新塑造音乐方向；从第一任妻子Naima作为穆斯林对其精神追求的启蒙，到第二任妻子Alice作为钢琴家与竖琴家在音乐上的协作。文章强调Coltrane并非刻意颠覆传统爵士，而是个人灵性、历史语境与时代潮流自然交汇的产物，他的演奏推开了Ornette Coleman等人曾虚掩的门，揭示了爵士乐情感表达与精神转化的内核。文中提及他对上帝的体悟如何直接转化为作曲养分，并以“我的目标是以音乐表达真正的宗教生活”引述其艺术哲学。整体更接近纪念性随笔而非音乐分析。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. items._cn_summary: 苏丹杜丹是来自挪威的二人组合，专辑以原声吉他为主导，辅以挪威传统乐器如小提琴、langeleik琴、lyre琴与口弦，织就八首带有深沉反思气质的作品。歌词以挪威语呈现，关切当下与未来，回望神话与谜语，涵盖大地日月星辰、失落与哀痛、想象力与古老谜题等意象。编曲并非一味阴郁，在轻快段落中融入了对法国知名旋律的解构重塑，以及源自无乐器伴舞场合的挪威传统tralling人声技法。终曲罕见地引入电吉他，深沉而带twang感的音色令人联想到杜恩·艾迪或大卫·林奇的配乐，为整张专辑画上意外句点。整体制作精良，想象力充沛，在北欧民谣传统根基上保留了独到的艺术个性。

items.body:
Though this recording documents the work of thirteen of Belgium's most innovative ensembles, the real star is the Park Abbey located just outside Leuven and founded in 1129. Built and maintained for the purpose of quiet meditation, the abbey hosted the musicians who used the quiet surroundings to prepare and record their unique musical imaginings. The result is a mostly instrumental collection that mines the riches of Belgian folk and world music traditions, including Romani scales,
La Pump
rhythms, and accordion-based
bal-musette
flavors.
For example, Slovenian-native R�n�lius Bikar�s searing violin opens the set with �R�fuge.� He and his self-named ensemble channel pan-European Roma history.
Meanwhile, �Poor Boy� is a Django Reinhardt-inspired swing tune by Charlotte Pelgen & Bipolar Bows. Pelgen sings in English, and with her ukulele strumming sounding very much like a tenor banjo, the tune is enlivened by Lotte Remmen�s St�phane Grappelli-like fiddle lines.
The distinctive sound of the oud announces yet another musical tradition. Blending Mediterranean with Arabic sounds, the Lebanese-Belgian singer Amber Haddad and her trio, oudist Adil Benhsain and double bassist Martijn Vanbuel, spin a beguiling musical web. According to the liner notes (translated from the Dutch), �Tawazden� is about �seeking balance and finding peace within a complex environment.� Further, �the various spaces of the abbey and their murals are the direct source of inspiration.�
The accordion is especially prominent. So too is the Western classical tradition. Sounding almost Baroque, �Sacristia Invisibilis,� is another standout for me. Here, mandolinist Andries Boone is joined by Anouk Sanczuk on octave violin (sometimes called the baritone violin, tuned an octave lower than standard) and on harpsichord Sandra Van der Gucht. They create an indescribable sound you have to hear.
Throughout, the Abbey�s stone presence looms. Aur�lie Charneux�s solo clarinet piece �L'Ape Millenaria� is about a thousand-year-old bee that haunts the abbey. �Thila,� by Enara Navaira, evokes ancient Celts with a jazzy double bass and drum kit behind throat singing and Citera (a kind of Hungarian zither).
Airboxes is a duo who mix chromatic and diatonic accordions. Their offering �Abdij 1� sounds improvised. Again from the liner notes, �they share their impressions of the timelessness of monastic life.�
Despite the wide range of styles,
The Sound of the Abbey
has a coherence, perhaps informed by the artists� shared inspiration. The record is often surprising and always soothing. Three years in the making, the ensembles were lovingly recorded and mixed by Bert Huysentruyt and mastered by Pieter De Wagter from Equus Mastering. They have rendered a warm sound using the natural reverb of ancient stone provided by the project�s silent partner.

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由乌克兰裔加拿大歌手Marichka主导，联合加拿大全女性团体Daughters of Donbas以及乌克兰本土乐手共同录制，以传统弓弦乐器、班杜拉琴、钢琴和双陶笛为载体，聚焦俄罗斯占领区约两万名被绑架儿童的主题。曲目融合传统民歌与原创作品，部分段落对古老仪式旋律进行再创作。歌词取材于乌克兰民间谚语和传统送别歌谣，将历史上女孩被迫离家做工的悲剧与当下儿童被强制迁移的现实相呼应。乐评人特别指出，专辑的音乐与演唱水准在乌克兰乃至世界音乐范畴内均属上乘，从纯音乐角度和了解歌词背景后的情感冲击两个层面都能产生强烈共鸣，整体呈现出克制而深沉的艺术表达。

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.
Tiny Sun -
Vanishment
(Review)
Carolina Chocolate Drops -
Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur合作完成，是该团体第五张作品，延续了他们与地下漫画家Robert Crumb长期合作的传统。专辑收录27首短曲，乐器阵容极为丰富，包括手风琴、萨克斯、木琴、单簧管、班卓琴、尤克里里、特雷门琴、夏威夷吉他、风笛及音乐锯等，呈现出从老式78转唱片中打捞出的复古质感。Cravic以近似说唱的唱腔演绎法国香颂与巴尔-缪塞特风格，同时融入拉格泰姆、罐乐队、skiffle等元素，形成难以归类的混搭美学。曲目涵盖对法国抵抗运动歌后Juliette Gréco的致敬，以及对经典老歌的重新编排。虽然整体偏向复古怀旧而非前沿实验，但其杂糅多源文化的拼贴手法和严肃的演奏态度，使其在跨界融合层面具有一定趣味。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?
items.label: Go' Danish Folk Music
items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合GuldGanger的首张数字EP，由北欧民谣场景中经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多基于传统音乐素材，融合锯琴、风笛、洋琴、长笛与弦乐等乐器，营造出古朴而略带粗粝的氛围。开场曲以起伏的节奏展示主唱嗓音的说服力；唯一原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，加入口簧与风笛的推进感；传统曲目中洋琴提供精致底色，口簧与弦乐交织出弹簧般的弹性尾奏。整体呈现成熟而有质感的传统民谣美学，但创新与跨界融合程度有限。作为北欧民谣与世界音乐交叉领域的作品，对关注民族音乐传统演绎的听众具有一定吸引力。

items.body: Manchester duo go big, vastly expanding their palette with strings, harps and a plethora of special guests Photograph credit: Timon Benson. Art Direction: Alexander Luc and Timon Benson. Clothing: Omar Afridi X VUJA DÉ There is a particular kind of light that only exists after rain has finished falling but before the sun has arrived – a grey-gold hour where the wet ground holds more colour than the sky. Space Afrika has always made records that live inside that hour. Honest Labour, the pair's breakout 2021 statement, was full of it: shortwave murmur, tower-block wind, the feeling of being simultaneously inside a crowd and entirely alone. Five years on, Joshua Tarelle Reid and Joshua Inyang return with Quiet Storm, a record that... The post Shared Frequency: Quiet Storm by Space Afrika appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Space Afrika作为曼彻斯特双人组，在Quiet Storm中大幅拓展了声音谱系，引入了弦乐、竖琴以及多位客座合作者。文章以雨后灰金色时刻的光线比喻切入，描绘他们音乐中始终存在的那种潮湿、幽暗而内向的氛围。回顾2021年的Honest Labour，短波收音机的低语、楼宇间的风声、身处人群却彻底孤独的质感，是他们一贯的创作基调。五年后的新作在此基础上进一步扩张，加入古典器乐编制与跨界合作，将电子质感与原声元素交织。从文风来看，评论以诗化意象引导读者进入听觉想象，但因原文篇幅极短，信息量有限，对新专辑的具体编排、制作理念或创新点的讨论尚未充分展开。整体呈现出从纯粹电子氛围向更复合化、编曲化方向演进的趋势，值得进一步聆听以判断其融合深度。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — A surprisingly-sophisticated and highly-entertaining album from a group of University of Illinois college students! Released on Brunswick Records in July of 1972.1. "The Monster Bride" (10:36) a very proggy, early King Crimson and Yes-like opening of bass, organ, clarinet, and delicate cymbal play turns in the second minute toward proggy brass rock--more like ELP meets BS&T. In the third minute the motif starts to smooth out before suddenly switching direction toward more light and playful circus music and then, in the fourth minute there is an equally sudden directional change toward more avant/eclectic Jazz-Rock Fusion before going Crimson and Zappa in the fifth. This is all quite tightly-performed and very sophisticated and unpredictable! It must have been something to compose and then pull off as a band in 1970s studio conditions. By the time we get to the end of the sixth minute everything slows down to a cymbal-supported droning organ for a Peter Hammill-like male vocal to enter and sing. Very Crimsonian! Flute and piano pick up from here with a very pretty, almost CHICAGO-like melody presentation and passage which builds and builds, horns entering and gathering forces over bass, guitar, and drum's rhythm track. At 5:22 everything stops for some percussion-backed dramatic very theatric narration of a sexually-piqued scene of the monster's reaction and response to the birth of his bride and child--which then leads to a finishing burst of CHICAGO-like brass rock. Very interesting! The sophistication of the compositions (and ability to pull it off in the studio) is the most impressive part. (18.375/20) 2. "Spiders (In Neals Basement)" (5:57) an accented male voice singing a sly lyric of film noir's detective-type music, like musical themes for scenes in a New Orleans juke joint or Chicago flop house. The music, performances both instrumentally and vocally are so colorful and spry. Great brassy theater music and great entertainment! Amazing that these were just a bunch of college kids! (9.333/10)3. "Witches Theme And Dance" (9:47) a brass rock song that opens like a LIGHTHOUSE song with great pace and energy before dropping down into a slow, plodding motif over which the gang issue some great four-part vocal harmony vocals. These guys must've done music theater or high school theater music. Bassist Neal Rosner is quite impressive (and, thankfully, placed forward in the mix), sounding a lot like Goblin or PFM's bassists. More stunning theatric stop-and-start composition performed with ease and professional precision over/within which electric guitar, voices, slide flute, and other mildly scary Hallowe'en noises contribute their solos and incidentals. Nice trilly flute solo in the final third--augmented by awesome "distant" flugelhorn. The finish is just perfect for the "lesson" of the witchy allegory. Another gem of a song; these guys are so creative and so talented! (18.875/20)4. "A Brief Message From Your Local Media" (9:59) here the band conjures up a four-part suite. It opens sounding like something from Aaron Copeland before organ, bass, hi-hat & bass drum lay down a soft carpet for a lone vocalist to begin his GREG LAKE-like "In the Court of the Crimson King" imitation. Obligatory flute joins in as "Greg" reaches his third verse--arpeggiated guitar chords and increasingly MICHAEL GILES-like drumming, as well. Around 4:30 there is a break in which narrator delivers a brief spoken-word summation of the contributions of Henry Ford to the workings of modern society, which is then followed by the development of a new motif of rather up-tempo organ- and flute-driven Jazz-Rock--which gains Latin elements in the eighth minute to give it a LEONARD BERNSTEIN West Side Story feel but then about a minute later the music moves more toward a pop/theatric-Brass Rock form similar to the snarky Hair, Godspel, and Pippen phenomenons. The music ends with a fading out calliope and military drums sound. Interesting. Though still delightfully creative and astonishingly sophisticated, the cohesiveness of this one is questionable (but, then, so is the flow of the typical radio or television programming!). (18.125/20) - a) "The Garden"- b) "The Assembly Line"- c) "Electric Man"- d) "Question"Total time 36:19Jazzy, brassy Crimsonian prog rock that sounds quite mature for a bunch of Illini students--and it's so entertaining, even addictive! Incredible for a debut album.A/five stars; a surprisingly-sophisticated and well-polished display of delightfully-entertaining compositions and performances. Who knew?! And, Whatever happened to?
items._genre: jazz rock / progressive rock / brass rock / fusion
items._cn_summary: MCLUHAN 的《Anomaly》是一张1972年由伊利诺伊大学学生录制的专辑，风格在爵士摇滚、前卫摇滚与铜管摇滚之间游走。首曲《The Monster Bride》长达十分钟，融合了管风琴、单簧管、铜管与打击乐，在King Crimson式的阴沉和Yes式的精致之间反复切换，中段插入戏剧化的旁白段落。贝斯手Neal Rosner的低音线条突出，接近意大利前卫乐队Goblin或PFM的处理方式。四部和声演唱、剧院式编排以及万圣节主题的氛围音效贯穿全作。整体展现了大学生乐手在录音室条件下完成的较为复杂的作曲能力，但风格仍偏向七十年代美式爵士摇滚传统，与用户偏好的实验前卫、学术爵士或电子音乐路线有一定距离。

items._cn_summary: 本乐评聚焦于作曲家 Kristine Tjøgersen 的作品，源自 Ultima Festival 2026 音乐节的现场报道。作者以巴伐利亚民间传说中沃尔珀丁格（Wolpertinger）这种由兔子、翅膀、鹿角、尾巴和獠牙拼接而成的虚构生物作为开篇比喻，暗示 Tjøgersen 的创作手法是将多种截然不同的音色与质感进行怪诞式的缝合与拼接。这种跨材质的拼贴手法属于当代古典与先锋实验音乐的常见策略，但乐评正文未提供更多关于具体作品结构、乐器编制或听觉细节的描述。整体而言，信息量极为有限，仅能确认其风格定位于实验性与当代古典的交叉地带。

items.album: BIOMES (2026; Chaikin)
items.excerpt: Katherine Young’s BIOMES project shows the composer thinking big, even when the sounds are quiet and sparse. A biome is a geographic region defined by its climate, vegetation, and wildlife. The concept is similar to that of an ecosystem, only on a larger scale. You don’t have to stretch far to find analogies to music-making. […]

A biome is a geographic region defined by its climate, vegetation, and wildlife. The concept is similar to that of an ecosystem, only on a larger scale. You don’t have to stretch far to find analogies to music-making. […]
items._cn_summary: Katherine Young 的 BIOMES 项目以生态群落的概念为出发点，将地理区域中气候、植被与野生动物的系统性关联映射到音乐创作中，探讨更大尺度上的声音生态隐喻。作品呈现"小而精"的美学取向——尽管声音编制限于安静与稀疏的范畴，创作者的构思却指向宏大的框架性思考。乐评将生物群落与生态系统的类比自然地引向音乐创作过程，暗示作曲本身即是一种有机的环境构建行为。专辑由 Chaikin Records 于 2026 年发行，属于独立小厂牌范畴，目前可获取的评论文本有限，无法深入了解具体配器与结构安排，但概念层面的艺术视角已展现出对实验音乐与声音艺术的明确取向。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自布鲁克林音乐人Semiratruth，被描述为对舞曲音乐的一次尖锐而令人惊艳的解构。从极短的文字来看，作品似乎聚焦于拆解舞曲的结构元素，以批判性或实验性的视角重新审视该类型，但具体的手法、音色选择和编排细节未能展开。位于纽约布鲁克林的独立音乐场景通常具备一定的实验氛围，然而文章本身更像是一篇Bandcamp Daily的预告或导语，而非完整的深度乐评，缺乏对制作理念、声音设计或音乐结构的深入分析。对于关注实验电子与解构性舞曲的听众而言，这张专辑可能是一个值得关注的对象，但现有信息不足以全面评估其艺术价值。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — In 1971, Biblical themes and rock operas were all the rage. This was David's contribution to the phenomenon. Though recorded in LA with a 38-piece orchestra (including bassist Carol Kaye, keyboard specialist Don Randi, and guitarist Mike Deasy), the lead vocalists are only listed as the singing group "The Dillons" while David's friend Julian "Cannonball" Adderley politely serves as the album's producer.A1. "Overture" (5:49) the first half is bombastic symphony orchestra, very well composed and rendered--like an overture. At the 2:45 mark there is a stoppage which is slowly filled by wah-wah-electric guitar, electric bass, funk-rock drumming, and dirty/raunchy electric piano as the orchestra horns and strings re-engage, only in more of a support/accent role--though their melodic presentation is continuous of those melodies presented in the opening half. Very cool! Very solid and well-rendered and powerful. (9.5/10)A2. "Comfort Ye My People" (2:45) Elton John-like solo piano opens this before male tenor voice enters to sing the words of the song's title. I really like this arrangement, the way David builds around Ed Dillon's singing and then start to increase in intensity and dramatic effect. (9.125/10)A3. "And The Glory Of The Lord" (4:50) like a rock-orchestra arrangement of a gospel choir rendering of this liturgical song. The vocal arrangements are quite rich and sophisticated; the rock instrumentation a little out of place. (9/10)A4. "Behold" (2:35) led by a Black female Gospel-Blues singer (a Dillon?), acoustic guitar is the only support instrument for the first minute--the first verse. Slow development brings in blues-rock instrumentation with orchestral horn support. Carol Kaye's bass and the electric piano are the most prominent of the rock musicians. Nothing very special or even dramatic here. (8.75/10) B1. "Pastoral Symphony" (5:35) layers of strings open this one, presenting the melody in a kind of fugue before more sections of the orchestra are slowly brought in. This sounds a bit like a New Age "spreading out" of a Pachelbel song. Nice but, again, nothing ground-breaking or exceptional. (8.75/10) B2. "And The Angel Said Unto Them" (2:52) opening with the same orchestral strings, in the second half of the first minute the music eventually gives way to a R&B combo for a Black female soprano gospel singer to sing over. The full orchestra is quite present, serving as thick and integral support, though the drums, bass, electric piano, and electric guitar work are the most active and aggressive here--especially in the song's second half--as anything else on the album. (Could that have been Earl Palmer on the drums?) (9/10) B3. "Glory To God" (3:03) elements of both female and male choirs are presented as opposed, woven, and antiphonal/echoing parts of the lyrical presentation while gentle funk-rock band and full symphonic orchestra participate from start to near-the finish. Quite a disciplined performance that David got out of these singers (as well as the orchestra). (9.125/10)B4. "Hallelujah" (3:23) we all know and love it. This one sounds like a slightly slowed-down, BARRY WHITE-version of the tune--until, that is, the second minute when the music moves into an all-instrumental section where Don, Mike, and the orchestra's horn section are given a little room to express themselves in solos. But then we return to the horn-embellished vocal delivery. I have to admit that I've heard many versions of this "song" that I like far better. (8.75/10)B5. "Worthy Is The Lamb" (2:52) nice Gospel choir music with totally-unnecessary and unfulfilling rock instrumentation. Even the orchestral work on this one feels as if it "gets in the way" of the fine vocal work. "The Dillons" are definitely a fine choir. (8.875/10)Total time: 32:40I have to say that this was one of the few times that I actually thought that the great Carol Kaye's bass playing was unbefitting to the music, which feels really weird since I revere her work and instincts so highly. Where I think David's work--his "Rock Interpretation"--started really strongly, I think it went off the rails somewhere in the middle of the Second Side. B+/4.5 stars; a near-masterpiece of the fusion of rock, jazz, R&B, and classical musical styles.
items._genre: crossover prog / rock orchestra / gospel rock
items._cn_summary: 大卫·阿克塞尔罗德1971年以38人管弦乐团为基础，将亨德尔的《弥赛亚》重新演绎为摇滚交响作品。编制上既有交响乐团的宏大编配，又融入放克摇滚节奏组、哇音吉他与电钢琴，形成古典与黑人音乐的跨界对话。部分曲目以福音唱诗班式的合唱呈现人声，奥本爵士的Julian Cannonball Adderley担任制作人。整体在宗教主题与摇滚歌剧风潮中寻求融合，编曲层次丰富，但评论者指出某些段落创新有限，摇滚乐器有时略显突兀。专辑展现了七十年代初洛杉矶录音工业对跨界融合的探索，在古典框架内引入节奏与黑人音乐语汇，是一种有意识的文化转译实验。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — Knowing that DANDO SHAFT was to add POLLY BOLTON as full time member for their eponymous 2nd album, I would have predicted such an infusion to be just what the doctor ordered for balance and groundedness. Paradoxically, this is a notably superior effort yet the 2 tracks on which she sings are among the weaker entries, not bad at all like the inane "Pass it on" but not nearly the equals of the authentic charms of the TIR NA NOG like ballad "Sometimes"; the lively spiritual endeavor of "Waves upon the ether", the sheer charm of "Whispering Ned", and the jaw dropping prog folk exuberance of "Kalyope Driver", their best by far to this point. The Anglo-Celtic flourishes are better integrated than on the debut even if they insist on weightlessly superficial 30 second interludes. A bonus cut on "An Evening with Dando Shaft" does suggest better things ahead with Ms. Bolton and indeed she may well have helped more than mere credits and front line contributions might imply. As you are discovering this unjustly suppressed talented collective along with me, I can only add that time will tell as we pivot freely through history from our advantage point.
items._genre: progressive folk / British folk / folk rock
items._cn_summary: 这是英国民谣乐队Dando Shaft的同名第二张专辑，评论者认为新成员Polly Bolton的加入本应为乐队带来平衡与沉稳，结果却呈现出一张整体优于首作的作品，但Bolton主唱的两首曲目反而成为专辑中较弱的环节。专辑亮点集中在几首器乐与人声交织的曲目中：Tir Na Nog风格的纯美民谣、活泼的精神性探索作品，以及充满前卫民谣活力的最佳曲目。评论指出凯尔特元素比首张专辑融合得更自然，但乐队仍执着于一些轻浮的半分钟间奏。整体而言，这是一支被低估的乐队在民谣与前卫边界上做出的有诚意探索，融合了英伦民谣传统与前卫摇滚的结构意识，但实验性有限，更偏向于精致编排的民谣摇滚范畴。
