items.body: Stabbing Westward Wither – ReWired COP International Re-recording a classic album is a risky proposition for any band or artist. Even leaving aside the shady practice of creating soundalike recordings to get in on streaming and sync royalties, the upside of recreating your own work is dubious; technically better performances, recording or production isn’t an improvement when a classic LP’s appeal is in familiarity, shortcomings and all. The best case scenario is that you come up with an interesting alternate take on your own material, but the more common outcome is sounding like a cover band. Thankfully, in the case of Stabbing Westward’s Wither – ReWired, a completely new version of the band’s 1996 breakthrough sophomore album Wither, Blister, Burn + Peel, the band have taken an approach that justifies the endeavor. Signed during the industrial rock’s brief moment of mainstream relevance in the 90s, the original record had catchy songs and benefited hugely from frontman Christopher Hall’s oh-so dramatic alt-rock vocals, but notably buried the majority of the band’s electronic elements beneath mountains of guitar chug. Wither – ReWired addresses that in a way that merely doing a new mix of the original tapes (if that were even an option) couldn’t, by not just recreating, but fully rearranging the songs to give the programming and synthwork equal billing. The results are striking in an A to B comparison of each version. Tracks that felt like lesser moments such as opener “I Don’t Believe” and “Crushing Me” are given a whole new life, the former by wedding a strong programmed rhythm section to the proceedings, the latter by upping the tempo and dialing back the original’s turgid guitars in favour of a sharp, forward moving arrangement. In the case of the record’s best and most memorable moments, such as the rock radio hit “What Do I Have to Do?”, things are left well enough alone, with minor tweaks to programming and the mix to keep it consistent with the rest of the record’s sound. In fact, they stick so close to how you expect those cuts to sound that the small changes stick out; Hall changes some of his vocal phrasing on the chorus to “Shame” in a way that feels wrong at first, but becomes comfortable after a few listens. The other important aspect of Wither – ReWired is in how its songs are sequenced as a listening experience. Where the 1996 original frontloads the record’s singles and most commercial cuts, the new version places songs in an order that feels like it makes more sense. “Slipping Away” is moved from the closing spot, its new club-ready iteration placed to pick things up from the mid-tempo melodrama of “Why?”, replaced by a revamped version of B-side “Agekata (Dawn)” whose more atmospheric synth textures better fit the role. “So Wrong” and “Inside You” (a deep cut that is secretly one of the band’s best moments) have significant time shaved off and are placed to keep the momentum and emotion of the record up leading into the final third. The amount of effort into making a genuinely new, but not unfamiliar album are considerable, and act as evidence that this is anything but a cash-in. Stabbing Westward could have churned out a quick and dirty version of their live set in studio and called it a day, but instead Wither ReWired is a genuinely considered undertaking by a band who understand who they were, who they are, and how to reconcile the thirty year gap in those incarnations. Buy it. Wither – ReWired by Stabbing Westward The post Stabbing Westward, “Wither – ReWired” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: 这是Stabbing Westward对1996年专辑《Wither, Blister, Burn + Peel》的完全重录版本，核心策略是将原本被吉他音墙压制的电子元素提升至与编程节拍、合成器音色同等地位。制作团队对歌曲结构进行了重新编排，例如放慢某些节奏、突出合成器纹理，使原本较弱的曲目获得新生命。对于原版标志性的热门单曲，则仅做细微的混音与编程调整，保留熟悉感。曲目顺序也被重新设计，弱化了商业单曲前置的策略，改为更具氛围连贯性的排列方式，将俱乐部导向的混音版与更具合成器氛围的B面曲调换位置。整体而言，这是一次对经典作品的有意义重塑，让电子工业基因获得了应有的表达空间。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源于艺术家在爱丁堡皇家植物园的驻留项目，以园中最古老的萨巴尔棕榈树被砍伐后意外发现其真实物种的故事为起点，构建出一部融合声音设计与钢琴人声的跨媒介作品。钢琴手Dave Milligan的演奏克制而富有同情心，与Polwart温暖包容的嗓音相辅相成，营造出亲密而庄严的氛围。歌曲旋律带有明显的苏格兰根源，开篇曲目犹如风笛低吟的挽歌。整体制作简洁，主要由人声、钢琴与精炼的声音设计构成，既具史诗般的自然与历史视角，又保持着内敛的尺度。专辑附带的书籍与现场演出延伸了音乐叙事，为这棵老树献上了配得上它的安魂曲，同时也寄托了对未来的希望。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑记录了Dr. John（Malcolm Mac Rebennack Jr.）1999年在德国Loreley露天剧场的演出，由WDR的Rockpalast音乐节目录制发行。乐队阵容精简，仅由吉他、贝斯和鼓组成四重奏，风格以新奥尔良传统为主轴，融合了R&B、布鲁斯、放克和迷幻沼泽摇滚元素。演出曲目涵盖Mardi Gras经典曲目如'Iko, Iko'和'Big Chief'，Dr. John的个人代表作如'I Walk on Guilded Splinters'、'Right Place, Wrong Time'、'Goin' Back to New Orleans'，以及Duke Ellington的翻唱作品。乐评强调其表演中带有巫毒仪式色彩的funknology风格，包括丛林咆哮、滑管哨音和迷幻吉他独奏。专辑本身既是经典档案记录，也适合作为新听众入门，演出跨越语言文化障碍，展现了新奥尔良音乐的普世感染力。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自芝加哥南区的田野录音作品，由录音师Ian Brennan在街头录制，二十五位枪支暴力幸存者口述亲身经历，涵盖从十七岁到六十七岁的参与者。录制地点位于中途机场降落航线下的社区，在一场葬礼旁进行，没有任何音乐添加，仅保留环境声与受访者的声音。作为一份现实记录而非传统音乐作品，它呈现出强烈的社会纪实属性，受访者的自发讲述构成主体内容。专辑收益将捐赠给致力于以公共卫生方法终结暴力的Cure Violence Global组织。从音乐角度而言，这与用户偏好的实验、爵士、电子等类型关联较弱，但作为声音艺术与田野录音的跨界实践，具备一定的实验性与社会意义。

items.body: Eight tracks, two of them longer than eight minutes and one past eleven: Fields of the Nephilim built their third album around length. Beggars Banquet released “Elizium” on 24 September 1990, two years after “The Nephilim” had taken the gothic rock band from Stevenage to number 12 in the UK. The new album peaked at number 22. It turns 36 this year, and it remains the last studio record by the line-up of Carl McCoy, Tony Pettitt, Peter Yates, Paul Wright and Alexander “Nod” Wright. The band recorded “Elizium” in 1990 at Park Gate Studios in Battle, East Sussex, with additional recording and mixing at Astoria in Hampton Court. Andy Jackson, the engineer on Pink Floyd‘s late-1980s records, produced the album with the band and engineered the sessions; Jon Carin added keyboards. McCoy wrote the lyrics and the five members share the music credits. The title respells Elysium, the afterlife of Greek religion, and “At the Gates of Silent Memory” opens with the voice of Aleister Crowley reading from his poem “At Sea” in a 1920 recording. Beverley Carruthers shot the front sleeve, and Sheer Faith and Chris Bigg designed the packaging. ‘Elizium’ tracklist, singles and reissues The album runs 48 minutes and 3 seconds: “(Dead But Dreaming)”, “For Her Light”, “At the Gates of Silent Memory”, “(Paradise Regained)”, “Submission”, “Sumerland (What Dreams May Come)”, “Wail of Sumer” and “And There Will Your Heart Be Also”. Beggars Banquet issued it in the UK on LP, CD and cassette, with Rebel Rec. and SPV handling the German-speaking countries. “For Her Light” came out as the lead single in July 1990 and reached number 54 in the UK; “Sumerland (Dreamed Version)” followed in November 1990 and peaked at number 37. Music On Vinyl repressed the album on LP in 2011. Beggars Arkive marked the 30th anniversary on 11 December 2020 with a 180-gram dark green vinyl edition, and on 5 April 2024 released an expanded double LP on brick red vinyl. That edition spreads the album over three sides and adds four tracks on the fourth: “Sumerland (Single Version)”, “For Her Light (Two)”, “Submission Two (The Dub Posture)” and “Sumerland (Dreamed Version)”. John Dent handled the analogue transfer and Sean Magee cut the vinyl master. About Fields of the Nephilim Fields of the Nephilim formed in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, in 1984 around vocalist Carl McCoy, bassist Tony Pettitt, guitarist Paul Wright, drummer Alexander “Nod” Wright and saxophonist Gary Wisker. Peter Yates joined on guitar in 1985, the year the band released the “Burning the Fields” EP on its own Tower Release label. Jungle Records reissued it and financed the “Returning to Gehenna” EP in 1986. Situation Two, the Beggars Banquet imprint, signed the band in 1986 and released the singles “Power” and “Preacher Man” ahead of the debut album “Dawnrazor” in May 1987. The second album, “The Nephilim”, followed on 5 September 1988 and entered the UK chart at number 12, with “Moonchild” reaching number 28 as a single. The stand-alone single “Psychonaut” peaked at number 35 in May 1989, and the band moved up to the parent Beggars Banquet label for “Elizium” in September 1990. The two-night Festival of Fire at London’s Town & Country Club in 1991 produced the live album “Earth Inferno”, released on 25 March 1991, and the concert video “Visionary Heads”. McCoy left later that year. Pettitt, Yates and the Wright brothers continued as Rubicon with singer Andy Delaney, releasing “What Starts, Ends” in 1992 and “Room 101” in 1995, while McCoy formed Nefilim, whose only album “Zoon” appeared in 1996. McCoy and Pettitt announced a reunion at the Zillo Festival in Germany on 15 August 1998. Jungle Records issued the single “One More Nightmare (Trees Come Down)” in May 2000 and, in October 2002, the album “Fallen”, compiled from 1997 to 2001 recordings and disowned by the band as unauthorised. “Mourning Sun”, the first new Fields of the Nephilim studio album since “Elizium”, came out on 28 November 2005. A new line-up returned to the stage at the London Astoria in May 2007 and headlined M’era Luna in 2008. The double live album “Ceromonies (Ad Mortem Ad Vitam)”, recorded at Shepherd’s Bush Empire, appeared on McCoy’s Sacred Symphony label in April 2012, and the single “Prophecy” followed on 17 March 2016. Guitarist Tom Edwards, a member from 2008 to 2016, died in January 2017, as Side-Line reported in Fields of the Nephilim / Adam Ant guitarist Tom Edwards dies aged 41. Beggars Arkive has since reissued the Situation Two and Beggars Banquet catalogue: the 30th anniversary “Elizium” in December 2020, an expanded “The Nephilim” in October 2023, the four-track expanded “Elizium” in April 2024 and a remastered “Dawnrazor” in December 2025. McCoy and Pettitt lead the current line-up with guitarists Gavin King and Adam Leach. Thirty-six years after its release, “Elizium” closes the first chapter of that catalogue, the final album of the original five-piece before “Earth Inferno” documented its last shows.
items._cn_summary: 本文是一篇纪念性质的新闻资讯文章，纪念Fields of the Nephilim第三张专辑《Elizium》发行36周年。文章以编年史式笔法详细记录了专辑的制作细节、录制地点、厂牌发行历史以及乐队成员构成，涵盖了从1984年乐队成立到2024年再版黑胶的全过程。文章没有对专辑的音乐内容、艺术成就或声音设计进行任何实质性的评论或分析，仅是事实性信息的堆砌。文中提到的制作人Andy Jackson曾与Pink Floyd合作，键盘手Jon Carin也参与了Pinky Floyd的录音，这为专辑带来了一定的氛围层次感。整体而言，这篇文字缺乏原创乐评深度，更接近于唱片档案条目，未能展现该专辑在暗潮与哥特摇滚领域的独特价值。

items.body: Boston gothic post-punk and deathrock band Gossip Collar has released “Eaten of Worms”, its third full-length album, on September 4, 2026 through Bat-Cave Productions. The ten-track record is available on CD and LP through the label, with a digital edition on Bandcamp. Eaten Of Worms by Gossip Collar ‘Eaten of Worms’ tracklist and credits Eaten of Worms was recorded and mixed by Marc Valois at Dead Moon Audio in Somerville, Massachusetts, and mastered by Jeff Lipton at Peerless Mastering in Boston. The album’s ten tracks are: Disguise My Heart Scavengers Big Top Comes Crashing Down Haerisis Dead Thing Why Me? Peaceful In Daylight Spelling Misery Unsafe State Merchants Of The Wave The record pairs electronic textures with serrated guitar work, running through recurring images of water, predatory animals and religious dread across its ten songs. CD and LP copies can be ordered directly through Bat-Cave Productions, with a download code included. About Gossip Collar Gossip Collar formed in Boston in the dark basement scene at the tail end of the pandemic, bringing together members previously involved with The Showcase Showdown, Spitzz and Secret Hearts. The band’s lineup is Victoria on vocals and guitar, Tom on guitar, Mark on bass and Megan on drums. Gossip Collar released a self-titled debut album on April 7, 2023, followed by spinning silk for parasites on October 31, 2024. Eaten of Worms, out September 4, 2026 via Bat-Cave Productions, is the band’s third album. Gossip Collar has performed alongside The March Violets, Pink Turns Blue, Rendez-Vous, Haunt Me, House of Harm, Fotocrime and Sympathy Flowers. Eaten of Worms extends that catalogue with the band’s most recent studio work to date. Follow Gossip Collar: – Bandcamp – Instagram
items._cn_summary: 波士顿乐队 Gossip Collar 发行第三张专辑《Eaten of Worms》，由 Bat-Cave Productions 厂牌推出 CD、LP 及 Bandcamp 数字版。专辑由 Marc Valois 在马萨诸塞州 Dead Moon Audio 录音混音，Jeff Lipton 负责母带处理。十首曲目将电子质感与锯齿状吉他交织，主题贯穿水、掠食动物与宗教恐惧的意象。乐队成立于疫情期间地下场景，成员曾参与 The Showcase Showdown、Spitzz 和 Secret Hearts，曾与 The March Violets、Pink Turns Blue 等同台。该文实质为专辑发行通告，仅列出版本信息、曲目清单与基本介绍，缺乏对音乐本身的评论与深度分析，信息密度较低。

items.album: Night Nail shares ‘Vile Train’ single from new album ‘Infinite Fountain’
items.excerpt: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail has released “Vile Train”, a gothic rock single that previews the band’s fourth studio album, Infinite Fountain, due November 6, 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The song arrives with an official video directed and edited by Jean De Oliviera. ‘Vile Train’ single details “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago, with co-production by Night Nail in Berlin and additional vocals and
items.body: Berlin-based darkwave act Night Nail has released “Vile Train”, a gothic rock single that previews the band’s fourth studio album, Infinite Fountain, due November 6, 2026 through Icy Cold Records. The song arrives with an official video directed and edited by Jean De Oliviera. ‘Vile Train’ single details “Vile Train” was mixed and post-produced by William Faith at 13 Studio in Chicago, with co-production by Night Nail in Berlin and additional vocals and guitar from VV & the Void. Frontman Brandon Robert said the track drew its initial inspiration from a visit to Pompeii, where a fresco depicting an angel and a demon in an embrace suggested “dark and brutal truths about love sung in a twisted but beautiful way.” The video reunites the band with director Jean De Oliviera, whose previous work with Night Nail includes “Hollow Day,” “Little Armenia” and “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher.” Shot in black and white, it cuts between Robert and bassist Ilija Gavrilenko performing among amplifiers and outdoor scenes set among stone arches and fountain basins. A full tracklist for Infinite Fountain has not been announced. The album also includes mixing and post-production work by Sven Wolff of Patenbrigade: Wolff. Night Nail plans to support the release with shows across the US, UK and Europe during 2026 and 2027. About Night Nail Night Nail formed in Los Angeles in 2013 and relocated to Berlin in 2018, the same year the band’s debut album, LA Demons, appeared on Cleopatra Records. March To Autumn followed in 2020 through Cold Transmission, and Fates Explained arrived on Metropolis Records in 2023, mixed and mastered by Pete Burns of Kill Shelter; Side-Line covered the single “Fates Explained” at the time. The band followed with the archival release Early Demons and Demos and the remix album Fates Remade in 2024, after earlier singles including “Narcoleptic Dream Catcher” and “Cracks In My Heart”, the latter featuring Luna De La Torre on vocals. Night Nail’s catalogue connects darkwave electronics with gothic rock’s appetite for emotional extremes, a combination built up over four albums and multiple labels since the band’s Los Angeles beginnings. “Vile Train” and the forthcoming Infinite Fountain, out on Icy Cold Records, mark the band’s next chapter and its first full-length since 2023’s Fates Explained. Follow Night Nail: – Bandcamp – Spotify – Website
items._cn_summary: Night Nail发布单曲《Vile Train》，作为其第四张专辑《Infinite Fountain》的预告。歌曲定位为哥特摇滚，混音与后期制作由芝加哥13 Studio的William Faith负责，并邀请VV & the Void参与和声与吉他录制。创作灵感来源于一次庞贝古城之旅，壁画中天使与恶魔相拥的意象被诠释为对爱情中黑暗而残酷真相的扭曲而美丽的表达。官方MV由Jean De Oliviera执导，黑白影像在功放设备间的室内表演与石拱门、喷泉池等户外场景间切换。乐队2013年于洛杉矶成立，2018年迁居柏林，曾先后与Cleopatra、Cold Transmission、Metropolis等厂牌合作，新专辑将通过Icy Cold Records于2026年发行。整体而言，这是一篇以资讯发布为主的新闻通稿，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评析。

items.body: The four-track release is out in November Richard Skelton and Lawrence English have teamed up for their first collaborative LP together, titled NOON. Comprised of four long-form tracks, the project came about from conversations that the two artists, on opposite sides of the world, had in 2021 about the volatile environments that they found themselves in, as Australia experience flooding and extreme weather, and Ireland's Atlantic coastline was hit by storms. In a joint statement, Skeleton and English said: “NOON operates as a palindrome of listening practices and experimentation, and moreover as a shared temporal marker that reminds us of the vastly finite turnings of our world." Watch a video for lead cut 'Sprites' below. Phantom Limb will release NOON on 20 November 2026. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nm_aRBrOMWg ... items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — David enters the House of Fantasy Records where the Mizell Brothers (Larry and Fonce) somehow convince David to arrange and conduct cover versions of famous hit songs from the realms of popular Jazz, Pop/Soul, and R&B music. Recorded at Fantasy Studios in March of 1974; released by Fantasy Records on July 1.A1."Get Up Off Your Knees" (3:38) a bluesy cover of a Julian Adderley composition--a song that had been previously recorded by Julian with his brother Nat--under the production of he and David!--back in 1971 where it was released as a 45 rpm single by Capitol Records. This version is a pretty straightforward, horn-dominated rendering of the familiar song. I don't really like it--the song or David's rendering.(8.667/10)A2. "Cast Your Fate To The Wind" (3:27) a flute and Fender Rhodes-dominated soft-jazz cover of Vince Guaraldi's classic Grammy Award-winning song from Vince's Trio's 1962 album, Jazz Impressions of Black Orpheus. This version from David and Julian is less than rousing despite the additional presence of a female choir for the final minute or so. (8.75/10)A3. "You're So Vain" (4:20) you really have to knock it out of the park for me to like an instrumental cover of a major hit song, but here David has Stephanie Spruill doing quite her own rendition of the main lyric--in full. I'm not even sure that Carly Simon would like, much less applaud, Stephanie's version. It's got an interesting, rather pulsing-yet-rubbery Moog bass line and near-Disco drum beat but Stephanie and the girls just take it too far for my comfort into the Black Funk territory of Betty Davis and Mavis Staples. (8.875/10)A4. "My Family" (4:45) the first of the Axelrod originals, it opens like a New Orleans funeral procession with baritone sax, trombone, and strings leading the melody. A big drum workup at 1:45 introduces the next level: one which is led by a steamy-hot electric guitar and swelling horns, but then, at 2:45 the music shifts into gear, thanks to Rudy Copeland's ultra-funky stretchy Moog bass line, congas, dreamy electric piano chords, and some sax from Gene Ammons. Interesting and cool but I'm definitely going to have to hear this one a few times before I can make head or tails out of it! (It's probably important to remember that David's family experienced a double trauma in 1944-5 with the passing of both his father and brother.) (9.125/10) B1. "Mucho Chupar" (3:13) one of David's four original compositions on the album, this song grooves like Deodato's "Super Strut," it moves, it coos and seduces, it swells and explodes. It is so fresh and innovative! That Moog bass is so killer! And the unexpected employment in the second minute of the female choir to express themselves in wordless Sirenese (a wordless Urszula Dudziak-Donna Summer-like ultra-seduction)--together and woven separately--is pure genius! Definitely my favorite song on the album. (9.375/10)B2. "Don't You Worry 'Bout A Thing" (3:45) a cover of the recent Stevie Wonder hit song, David chooses to have flutes, strings, and George Duke's Fender Rhodes lead the melody recreation while the rock band and orchestra helps out lightly (other than the flutes) for the first two minutes. The second minute really lets George shine, but then strings, electric guitar, and horns begin to swell and make the song much fuller--until an unexpected fadeout terminates the song. Just when they were starting to cook! (8.875/10)B3. "It Ain't For You" (4:25) the third of David's compositions is quite funky with "Guitar" Watson, George's clavinet, Rudy Copeland's Moog, and Roy McCurdy's crisp drums filling the sonic field with the help, for a while, of David's background horns. The guitar, clavinet, and Moog are the main players, the main attraction--what an amazing Moog bass Rudy (or George) is playing! Mixed with the clavinet and rhythm guitars it makes for such a stinky funk! More like this, please! My only (small) criticism here is that there is a bit of a BILLY PRESTON's "Outa-Space" familiarity/feel to this. (9.333/10) B4. "Everything Counts" (6:54) the album's fourth and final original composition opens with bluesy organ and stretchy Moog bass mixing it up before drums and orchestra horns and then full orchestra add their own melodic accents (much in the dramatic pattern and style that David has been championing since his debut album in 1968). That bass is amazing! Left alone with King Errisson's congas it makes for the closest thing I've ever heard to Tony Levin's ChapmanStick playing! George tries to fill space above the rhythm section with some nice, laid-back Fender Rhodes play but it takes the horn section blasts and/or bluesy electric guitar soloing to do anything to draw my attention away from that Moog-led rhythm section! (13.625/15) Total time: 34:16A-/4.5 stars; what may be a minor masterpiece of Funk-Jazz is probably just a near-masterpiece of Jazz-Rock Fusion.
items._cn_summary: 这是制作人David Axelrod于1974年发行的专辑，由Mizell兄弟制作，邀他在Fantasy录音室改编并指挥流行爵士、灵魂乐与节奏蓝调的经典曲目。专辑收录了Julian Adderley、Vince Guaraldi、Stevie Wonder等知名作品的器乐翻唱版本，并穿插Axelrod的原创作品。编曲以铜管乐器、Flute、Fender Rhodes和Moog合成器贝斯线为核心，部分曲目加入女性人声合唱。Axelrod的原创新奥尔良葬礼游行式的开场段落结合funk律动，呈现出一定程度的实验色彩，但整体仍偏向七十年代跨界爵士流行的制作框架，与极端前卫或即兴路线距离较远。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — In the early 2000s, Savatage's core members were juggling their time and musical ideas between the band and the increasingly demanding side project Trans-Siberian Orchestra, created by Jon Oliva, producer Paul O'Neill, and arranger and keyboardist Robert Kinkel. It was against this hectic backdrop that the American band released "Poets and Madmen" (2001), their eleventh album, whose central theme revolves around a loose adaptation inspired by the tragic fate of Kevin Carter, the photographer who captured the harrowing image of a Sudanese child crouching on the ground, watched from a short distance by a vultur - a photograph that earned him the Pulitzer Prize in 1994.The album features the return of Oliva's raw and expressive voice as lead singer, a greater prominence of Chris Caffery's rhythmic and heavy guitar riffs, and a solid instrumental foundation, supported by Kinkel's symphonic arrangements. All of this lends, on the one hand, that combination of theatrical stage presence and razor-sharp energy characteristic of metal outbursts in tracks like the anguished "Stay with Me a While", the martial "Commissar," and, above all, the epic "Morphine Child", an elaborate and highly fluid epic that includes superb choral segments and is surely the jewel of the album.On the other hand, there's room to revisit the genre's raw, primal roots with the fast-paced, '80s-style heavy track "Drive"; the density of doom metal with Sabbath-esque touches in "I Seek Power" - another great track - ; and the pasty "Awaken," with Oliva on the verge of vocal breakdown. There are also some acoustic subtleties in hybrid tracks like "The Rumour (Jesus)" and "Man on the Mirror", where the band navigates peaceful valleys and abrupt instrumental mood shifts with great skill.The self-indulgent and theatrical "Got to Get Back to a Reason" - a track that attempts to capture the emotion in the air and give the album an epic, redemptive ending - ends up also being the final piece in the band's discography. Because, despite the musicians' intention to maintain both projects simultaneously, their packed schedules and commitments made their coexistence unsustainable. After the album's promotional tour and in the absence of an official statement, Savatage went on a "hiatus" that has now lasted 25 years...3.5/4 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / heavy metal / theatrical metal
items._cn_summary: 这张2001年的专辑以南非摄影师凯文·卡特的真实悲剧为叙事核心，将人道主义议题融入金属乐的戏剧化框架。制作层面回归主唱奥利瓦粗粝而富有表现力的人声，配合吉他手克里斯·卡弗里厚重节奏化的riff以及键盘手金克尔的交响化编曲，呈现出舞台剧般的张力与金属爆发力。作品横跨多个情绪光谱——从急促的八十年代风格金属到带有黑色安息日影响的厄运金属段落，再到民谣式原声吉他穿插的冥想段落，配以合唱段落与出人意料的器乐转向。专辑作为乐队实际上的收官之作，试图以史诗性、救赎式的终曲为整体画上句号。尽管乐队在交响化编排与多段式叙事结构上展现了相当的编曲功底，但整体仍属传统前卫金属范畴内的精致制作，与用户所关注的实验前卫、学院爵士、电子、世界音乐及暗潮等方向存在明显距离。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — Despite having been around for some thirty years (their first album, released in 1993, was produced by Eroc, former drummer of Grobschnitt), very little has been written about this German band in the progressive music press, with the exception of a few wonderfully insightful reviews published in 2001 to mark the release of their masterpiece, *Fantasma*. In those insightful lines, everything was said?from the impeccable vocals of Oliver Philipps?the heart and soul of the band?which stir us with emotion in airy, nostalgic atmospheres, to Everon's distinctive taste for Rush at its most melodic. Incidentally, the influence of the fathers of Canadian hard-prog on a band from our good old continent is rare enough to warrant special mention. For good measure, among the similarities or influences more or less acknowledged by Everon, we should also mention the prog metal of Vanden Plas, the even more symphonic style of Sylvan, or the more neo-prog sound of Pallas. And despite my fear of intriguing or horrifying some readers, I'll also take the liberty of pointing out Oliver Philipps's avowed fondness (see his website) for Nik Kershaw.But it's through a subtle affinity for Rush that *North* really bursts onto the scene, with a mind-blowing and compact "Hands ", driven by an unstoppable melody yet free of any lulls or orchestral flourishes (here, a few keyboards with a discreet but essential presence)?exactly as Oliver Philipps intended, having momentarily had his fill of his own sumptuous arrangements.A track remarkable for its ability to encapsulate the very best of its creator's aspirations, "Hands" reassures us of Everon's intentions: to succeed in creating something that is both simple and grandiose. This is something the band's two previous albums, *Flesh* and *Bridge*?which were not substantial enough despite the extravagant 14-minute title track "Flesh"?partially failed to achieve; curiously, both were released in the same year (2002). The next track, "A Brief Encounter", is the biggest surprise on the new album: constructed like a sort of "Turn of the Century" in tune with our times (read: with a testosterone boost), complete with acoustic guitar and piano parts, it unabashedly reveals the depth of Philips' love for the universal sound of Yes. The greatest (and consistent) melodic shortcoming?at least on the early albums?has, over time, become a strength. Straight to the point: emotion. UnforgettableOliver is a tremendous singer who has never stopped improving since a debut album that was nearly disastrous in that regard (a young Greg Lake's voice, uncertain and poorly anchored to confusing melodies) to reach a level that only the very best have attained. On that note, on *North*, be sure to listen to "Test of Time", opulent prog metal with a brief cello intro. Or the tormented "North" ("I remember I wrote 'North' on an unbelievably stormy day" (O. Philipps), with its false string section richer than a cathedral door.Olivier Philipps is also an excellent musician (guitars, keyboards) who puts his performance at the service of the richness of the melody?and not the other way around. He's fairly sparing with solos but increasingly generous with pure emotion, as on "Wasn't It Good" (6:33), the most poignant track on *North*, my favorite track, and probably also Oliver Philipps's favorite on this album: "Actually, in my humble personal opinion, this kind of song is the essence of what Everon is all about" (O. Philipps). At the beginning, with a touch of nostalgia, a piano begins to float heavily through the ether, the melody detached from its harmonic body, a sphere of thought undulating at the end of a long string. And when the guitar solo comes in?which seems as simple as pie, so much so that even my thick, clumsy little fingers think they can play it?you find yourself hoping never to hear another lukewarm review of Everon.The edgy "Woodworks", a highly successful instrumental, as if to retrospectively disprove the famous review mentioned above, which noted that instrumentals had never been Everon's strong suit (a claim already contradicted at the time by the intro to "Venus" in 1997, as beautiful as anything by Dave Bainbridge), helps lighten the emotional load somewhat after bringing us to our knees. And Judith St�ber's enchanting voice on the ballad "Islanders" gently lifts us back up. And we stand tall as we listen to the glorious and energizing "Running", convinced that *North* is a truly ambitious album, a classic?and not just another heavy prog record?a formidable magnetic force that, while not reaching the absolute pinnacle of modern progressive rock, succeeds where so many others have failed, starting with Everon himself up to this point: to bring together in a single artistic work 10 crisp, simple, and clear melodies, set in 10 rings of precious metal, resting on 10 harmonic velvet cases. With the uncertain style of their early days having given way to a confident musical personality, Everon's music?that of their new album in particular?can fulfill the deepest progressive aspirations hidden within us. There's no doubt that *North* could give Everon the place it deserves: on the podium. At last!
items._genre: heavy progressive rock / neo-prog / prog metal
items._cn_summary: 这张2008年的专辑由德国老牌前卫金属乐队Everon发行，乐评着重分析乐队主唱Oliver Philipps的人声演变轨迹——从早期类似年轻Greg Lake般的不稳定音色，逐步成长为兼具情感深度与旋律掌控力的歌手。评论将乐队定位为Rush的欧洲追随者，同时承认Vanden Plas、Sylvan、Pallas等乐队的影响，并提及Philipps对Nik Kershaw的偏爱。专辑曲目如Hands追求简洁宏大的对立统一，Test of Time呈现饱满的前卫金属编制，North则以弦乐铺陈营造戏剧张力。从用户口味出发，这类重型前卫摇滚虽属前卫范畴，但偏向传统旋律化路线，缺乏实验性元素、爵士融合、电子声响或暗潮氛围，与实验/前卫/爵士/电子等核心偏好存在明显距离。评论本身信息丰富但与用户审美方向错位。

items.body: Tanner McGraw sings and John Beckmann stays off the microphone on “Nothing Is Missing”, the third single from Utopia PKWY, out on 25 September 2026 with a video. Utopia PKWY is the new project of Beckmann, the New York songwriter and producer behind The Mortal Prophets, and the single precedes the project’s first album, “Debut”, due on 6 November 2026. Beckmann wrote and produced the track alone; McGraw takes the lead vocal and Lawson Mars adds backing vocals. Utopia PKWY mix post-pop hooks with synth-wave-tinged psychedelia, and bring keyboards, theremins and sitars into the arrangements. The single follows “I Knew You Would Be Trouble”, released on 3 July 2026, and “Sleep In Moving Colors”, released on 14 August 2026, both with official videos on the project’s YouTube channel. The “Nothing Is Missing” video was not yet public at the time of writing, so the player below carries the second single, whose video upload is titled “I Sleep In Moving Colors”. Beckmann described the new song as “Less a song than a philosophical hallucination, more like a midnight transmission from the far side of grief – where loss doesn’t disappear, it simply changes frequency and keeps humming beneath the skin.” The project takes its name from Utopia Parkway in Queens, the street where the Surrealist artist Joseph Cornell lived and worked. Beckmann calls McGraw and Mars, his two younger collaborators, the “kids in the neighborhood”. Both singers already appeared on the two most recent psychedelic dream-pop albums by The Mortal Prophets, and Utopia PKWY moves that line-up into brighter, more melodic songs. ‘Debut’ tracklist and release dates “Debut” runs to ten tracks: “I Knew You Were Trouble”, “Sleep In Moving Colors”, “Nothing Is Missing”, “If I Could Steal One More Kiss”, “You Talk Like Every Feeling”, “What Disappears”, “Come In Waves”, “Glitter And Doom”, “Fall Into You” and “Dreaming I’m A Rock Star”. The tracklist spells the opener “I Knew You Were Trouble”, while the single and its video carry the title “I Knew You Would Be Trouble”. The closing title also appears on The Mortal Prophets’ July 2026 album “Ain’t No Fool”. The earlier Utopia PKWY singles are on Spotify and Apple Music; the album page on the official site lists the release dates for all three singles and the album. About Utopia PKWY Utopia PKWY is the 2026 side project of John Beckmann, a New York singer, songwriter, producer and visual artist who has recorded as The Mortal Prophets since 2022. That project opened with the EP “Stomp The Devil” on 8 July 2022 and the album “Me And The Devil” on 9 December 2022, both built on reworked blues standards. “Dealey Plaza Blues” followed on 28 July 2023, the ambient guitar album “Guitarworks” on 22 December 2023, the EP “Sleeping In My Bed” on 15 March 2024, the opera “Hanussen: The Enigmatic Clairvoyant” on 15 April 2024, the EP “ICNCLST/” on 20 August 2024 and “Laurel Canyon – Lost Sessions (1966-69)” on 29 November 2024. In 2025 came “Ghost Land” (17 January), “French Summer” (16 May), “Guitarworks II” (28 July) and the covers EP “Under The Influence” (5 December). The move toward dream-pop and psychedelia began with “Hide Inside The Moon”, released on 2 January 2026, the first Mortal Prophets record with Tanner McGraw on lead vocals. “Not Here, Not There” followed on 3 April 2026 with McGraw and Lawson Mars sharing the vocals over synth-wave keyboards, theremins and sitars, and “Ain’t No Fool”, with Jake Burden on vocals, arrived on 3 July 2026. On the same day Beckmann launched Utopia PKWY with “I Knew You Would Be Trouble”, again with McGraw and Mars singing, and released “Sleep In Moving Colors” on 14 August 2026. “Nothing Is Missing” on 25 September 2026 is the last single before “Debut” on 6 November 2026.

items.body: IAMX, the solo project of Chris Corner, is running a silent auction of two stage-used items from the 2026 “Recollections” tour: a bass guitar played on stage by touring bassist Gözde Düzer and a rhinestone-covered mask worn by Corner during live shows. Both auctions close on 27 September 2026 at midnight CEST, while the tour is mid-way through a run of Scandinavian dates. The bass guitar was played on stage by Gözde Düzer, who tours as IAMX’s bassist and also records as Aux Animaux. It is signed by both Düzer and Corner and comes in a hand-stencilled hard case made for the tour. The second item is a handmade mask Corner wore onstage throughout the “Recollections” shows, covered in rhinestones with black fur ears and gold detailing. Both listings are running through the band’s official shop and close at midnight CEST on 27 September 2026. IAMX tour dates for 2026 and 2027 23 September 2026 – Oslo, Norway – John Dee 24 September 2026 – Malmö, Sweden – Plan B 25 September 2026 – Helsinki, Finland – On The Rocks, with Aux Animaux 13 November 2026 – Santiago, Chile – Santiago Gothic Treffen 14 November 2026 – São Paulo, Brazil – Madame Club 24-25 July 2027 – Cologne, Germany – Amphi Festival 31 July – 1 August 2027 – Thale, Germany – Unter dem Himmel About IAMX IAMX is the solo project of British musician Chris Corner, who co-founded the trip-hop group Sneaker Pimps in Hartlepool in 1994. After a fourth Sneaker Pimps album went unreleased, Corner kept the songs, moved to London and released them as the debut album “Kiss + Swallow” in 2004. Later albums include “The Alternative” (2006), “Kingdom of Welcome Addiction” (2009), “Volatile Times” (2011), “The Unified Field” (2013), “Metanoia” (2015), “Unfall” (2017), “Alive In New Light” (2018), the acoustic rework album “Echo Echo” (2020) and “Machinate” (2021), followed by “Fault Lines¹” (2023) and “Fault Lines²” (2024). IAMX opened 2026 with the single “Artificial Innocence” ahead of a European tour, and Corner discussed his songwriting approach in a Side-Line interview in May. Gözde Düzer, who tours with the band on bass and theremin and records on her own as Aux Animaux from Stockholm, spoke to Side-Line in March about joining the IAMX live band and touring with Chris Corner. The “Recollections” tour has since carried the band through Scandinavia this week, with dates in Chile and Brazil to follow in November and festival shows at Amphi Festival and Unter dem Himmel booked for the summer of 2027. This week’s silent auction of stage props from the tour runs alongside that live schedule.

items.body:
Thailand has a new rock star to celebrate.

Nene Royal, the 16-year-old guitarist and singer from Phuket, has been crowned the winner of America’s Got Talent Season 21, becoming the first Thai contestant to win the long-running competition.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by America's Got Talent - AGT (@agt)

Ahead of the results announcement, Nene joined Linkin Park onstage for 'The Emptiness Machine', playing guitar and trading vocals with the band’s Emily Armstrong.

The performance capped off a breakout run on the show for Nene, whose real name is Rattikarn Amloy. For the finals, she delivered a heavy rendition of The White Stripes’ 'Seven Nation Army'. Throughout the competition, she also performed Soundgarden’s 'Black Hole Sun' and The Cranberries’ 'Zombie', with the latter earning her widespread attention after her audition went viral.

Nene also jammed with Mexican rock trio The Warning during the finale.

Before making it onto America’s Got Talent, Nene started playing guitar at seven and performed as a street musician in her hometown of Phuket, including busking at the city’s Naka Weekend Market. She has since built an online following through her performances on YouTube.

Following her victory, Nene thanked everyone who supported her, saying: “I’m very happy and emotional right now.”

As the season’s champion, Nene takes home US$1 million and earns a showcase on the Las Vegas Strip.

items.body:
Ben&Ben are celebrating nine years of music and memories with their new anthology album, Nine.

Out now via Sony Music Entertainment, the nine-track record revisits key moments from the Filipino folk-pop band's journey through newly reimagined versions of their songs, alongside the brand-new track 'Harinawa'. Rather than simply looking back, Nine captures how the group and their music have evolved after nearly a decade together.

“Reimagined, for us, is letting the songs grow up with us,” shared lead vocalist and acoustic guitarist Paolo Benjamin. “Our Liwanag, and we the band too, were molded by life a lot in the past nine years.”

The anthology's focus track, 'Maybe the Night (Reimagined)', takes the band back to one of their earliest milestones. Originally arranged in Jam Villanueva's attic in 2017, 'Maybe the Night' was the first song the members worked on collectively from start to finish as a nine-piece.

For the new recordings, Ben&Ben drew from years of performing together, bringing the energy and chemistry of their live shows into the studio. Poch Barretto led the album's full production, with longtime collaborator JP Verona and producer Ziv also contributing to the project.

Closing the anthology is 'Harinawa', a new song written and completed during the band's ninth year. Carrying a message of hope and positivity, the track points towards the group's next chapter.

“We hope for these nine songs to accompany [Liwanag and our listeners] wherever they’re at in their lives right now,” shared Toni Muñoz. “Hope comes in many forms, and we wish for our music to be even just a glimpse of one of them.”

items.body: Review by Finnforest — "Sitting at Dawn, Watching" The second of the Salis brothers' trilogy of 1970s albums was released in 1974. All three of theiralbums are entirely different from one another, each one interesting in its own way. The first albumfrom 1970 was essentially proto-RPI, a mix of Italian pop with heavier and more boisterousovertones. For this second release, well into the classic first wave RPI, we get an album that issurprisingly softer, mellower, a bit less focused and less earnest perhaps, but not without its owncharms. Surprisingly, I say, because this is the moment ('74) where you'd expect them to gobarreling into their prog rock opus, but they do not. This album has less of a rock band feel (progor otherwise) and more of a singer-songwriter vibe with gentler vocal-oriented tracks comprised ofacoustic guitars and plenty of flute for dessert. Perhaps there is some influence of the LaurelCanyon folk rock scene, perhaps not, but the material is going to appeal to anyone who enjoysSouthern Cal acoustic rock, I suspect, and yet the album also has moments of soft symphonic and, ofcourse, Italian flavor as well. Drums and bass take a substantially supportive role here. Harmony vocals are used effectively to addlushness. Even keyboards, while present throughout, take a less prominent role than the acousticguitar playing, which is truly excellent and interesting throughout. On tracks like "Un Uomo," theystill break into a more spirited and jazzy feel with active organ and bass driving the song, but italmost never moves into riskier or avant-garde territory. Some reference points for this secondalbum (only) would include Era Di Acquario, Mario Barbaja, and even Battisti. While the "progquotient" may be relatively low here, this is still a fine album that will appeal to fans of Italy'slovely music tradition. It also benefits from a great production and top-notch sound.
items._cn_summary: 这是意大利Salis兄弟1974年发行的第二张专辑，处于经典第一波意大利前卫摇滚时期，却出人意料地走向柔和而非典型的前卫摇滚方向。整张专辑以原声吉他为核心，辅以长笛点缀，键盘存在感较低，鼓与贝斯仅作支撑。嗓音为主导，采用和声人声增加层次感。部分曲目如《Un Uomo》展现了一定的爵士化活力，加入管风琴推动，但整体并未进入冒险或前卫领域。乐评特别指出其'前卫系数'较低，更接近歌手创作人风格，或许受到美国南加州民谣摇滚的影响。专辑具备优异的制作与音质水准，对意大利音乐传统的爱好者仍有吸引力，但实验性与前卫性极为有限。

items.body: 24. September, vor 60 Jahren. Jimi Hendrix landet in London. 24 Jahre alt, in seiner Heimat USA ein Nobody. In London aber ist Hendrix schnell eine Sensation. Spielerisch, kompositorisch; die Breaks und Arrangements, die Show, die Ausstrahlung, Afro-Aura, das Wie. Wie er die Gitarre behandelte, misshandelte, keine Töne spielte, sondern fühlte und weiterhauchte, Akkorde und Noten ineinander verkuppelte wie in einem wild zerrupften Kingsize-Bett. Hoch-konzentriert und dann wie ein aus einem Wanderzirkus flüchtender 5-jähriger.Keine vier Jahre später, am 18. September 1970,  wird Hendrix’ – vermutlich – kaum mehr lebender Körper vom Samarkand Hotel zum St. Mary Abbots Hospital gebracht, wo der diensthabende Notfallarzt nach Wiederbelebungsmaßnahmen um 12:45 Uhr den Tod des Amerikaners feststellt. So weit, was wie Fakten klingt.   Im HHV Shop kaufenThe Jimi Hendrix ExperienceAre You Experiencedab 24.99€Jimi HendrixMagic Boy: The Jimi Hendrix Experience Live At Berkeley First Showab 34.99€The Jimi Hendrix ExperienceWinterlandab 31.99€Jimi HendrixElectric Ladyland 50th Anniversary Deluxe Editionab 104.99€Die Platten von Jimi Hendrix findest du im HHV-Shop Geil und aufregend Daten sind ja viel wert. Zahlen auch. Selbst wenn man genau darüber das Phänomen Jimi Hendrix am allerwenigsten erfasst, über das Messbare. Ausweislich der Plattenverkäufe in den USA (RIAA Buchführung) kommen Hendrix‘ drei zu Lebzeiten aufgenommenen Studioalben auf 10 Millionen; alleine Thriller wird mit Mio. 34 gelistet, Hotel California mit 28 Mio., Back in Black mit 27 Mio., Led Zeppelin IV mit 24 Mio., The Wall mit 23 Mio. Hendrix hat seinen Status als Legende nicht wegen der Zahlen inne. Zurück ins Jahr 1966. Die neu gegründeten Cream machten als Trio den aus den USA importierten Blues rockiger, auch – analog zu Jazz – anspruchsvoller. Fast sophisticated. Und während es bei Elvis, Beat und Pop um 7“-Singles, schnelllebiges Zeug zum Mitpfeifen und Vergessen ging, kam nun die Langspielplatte. Beatles‘ Revolver zerschoss Karrierekorsetts des alten Musters. Farbe fand ins Fernsehen. Das Raumschiff Enterprise hob ab; Jane Fonda ging weiter: sie sauste in Barbarella mit Stones-Muse Anita Pallenberg und Marcel Marceau ins Jahr 40.000. Die Zukunft, alles Kommende war noch geil und aufregend, voller Möglichkeiten. Die Sinne der Massen sensibilisiert, kam 1967 Beatles‘ Sgt. Peppers mit Klappcover. Das Album als Gesamtkunstwerk. Wie ein ausgerollter roter Teppich für Hendrix‘ Debüt Are You Experienced?. Das Album erschien im Mai 1967. Kein Jahr nach seiner Ankunft in London also. Wo er Tage nach seiner Landung noch in Clubs jammte, dann Vorgruppe für Cream spielte, gefolgt von mehreren Dates in Frankreich und der Münchner Diskothek Big Apple. Zu Pfingsten war er Headliner in Berlin. Zum Preis von drei Schachteln Zigaretten, DM 6,– Eintritt, im Vorverkauf.  »Einmaliges Sondergastspiel, Jimmy Hendrix mit The Experience aus London«. Einer Zeitzeugin zufolge, Absolventin der Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics, verliefen sich, fußläufig vom Club Neue Welt, mehrere Besuchende – unter ihnen der 68er-Kult-Autor Bernward Vesper mit seiner Lebensgefährtin Gudrun Ensslin in der Hasenheide. Tagelang. Der Beginn des Spektakels Inzwischen tritt Hendrix eigentlich nonstop auf, auch in den USA, auch mit The Who, im Package mit Cat Stevens, spielte um die 400 Mal, an manchem Tag auch zwei Gigs. Parallel nahm Hendrix‘ Trio weiter im Studio auf. Mit mobilen Endgeräten, mitnehmbaren Schallplattenspieler, der es ihm erlaubte, drei Tage nach dem bahnbrechenden Beatles-Album den Titelsong zu spielen. Spieltechnik ständig am Reifen, aber auch die Technik, die das Massenphänomen begleitet. Sichtbar ist, dass er sich früh Boxen der P.A.-Firma WEM auf die Bühne stellt, die im Heavy Metal heute normativen Marshall-Türme ordert er bei Jim Marshall, dem ehemaligen Lehrer des Experience-Drummers Mitch Mitchell.   Das alles – Musik voller Energie und Lärm und nuancierten Gänsehautmomenten – vor kontinuierlich größeren Zuschauermengen. Explosiv und aufflammend im Finale bei Monterey Pop (dem ersten Baby des Summer of Love), abgeklärter und überwältigt kulminierend in Woodstock, wo Hendrix als Haupt-Attraktion auftrat. Für 500.000 in Woodstock wurde die Soundanlage fürs Publikum unglaublich professionalisiert. Um die 10.000 bis 12.000 Watt auf 16 Lautsprecher-Türmen, Speaker separat ausgerichtet auf die nahestehenden und die entfernteren Fans. Verantwortlich zeichnete sich der Mann, der beim Newport Jazz Festival am Mischpult stand, als die Jünger Bob Dylan ausbuhten, weil er zur E-Gitarre gewechselt war. Small world. Im Grunde war das, fand man später, die Blaupause für Mega-Spektakel-Events, der Übergang vom Beat-Treiben hin zum Big Business, speziell mit Solokünstlern, die sich leichter lenken lassen als Bands. Und die Person Hendrix, zwischen all dem? Charmanter Talker, schüchtern, charismatisch. Voller Gegensätze. Wie die ultra-krachenden Attacken neben Arrangements, flüssig wie ein Bach. Zudem war er offenbar ein Intensiv-Zuhörer, der analysierte, sofort nachahmte, was es wert war, mitgenommen zu werden; der verbesserte und alles lauter und elektrifiziert zurechtstutzte – wie in Unterhaltungen jeder Gitarrismus-Gitarrist herausfand. Ähnlich äußerten sich auch Joni Mitchell, Frank Zappa, Bob Dylan, Beatles, Pete Townshend. Schnell in der Auffassung, polyamourös mit Hörgewohnheiten. Voll da. Verstärker und Technik, Effekte und Astraltheorien, alles gleich aus den Vollen gekippt. So viel wie Hendrix verdiente zu der Zeit kein Musiker, auch keine Band, auch nicht Dylan oder Elvis. Kohle beiseitelegen oder unterschlagen konnten bis zu vier Manager gleichzeitig. Hendrix war umgarnt von Abstaubern und Nachtfaltern, Alles-Checkern und Blutegeln. Die Gitarre brennt ja sowie schon Knapp nach seinem 56.–Todestag – 18. September – kommentiert irgendwer auf YouTube: »Einfach absolut erstaunlich: Er starb 1970 und schuf in seinem kurzen Leben über 170 Songs – und hier sind wir im Jahr 2026, und Jimmy ist immer noch unerreicht. Sein Werk und sein Können waren ein wahres Meisterstück. Er verließ diese Welt als geliebter Mensch, und sein Schaffen wurde gut bewahrt. Seiner Eigenheiten war er sich bewusst und spannte die Saiten seiner Gitarre deshalb ganz bewusst verkehrt herum auf – damit auch lange nach seinem Tod niemand seine Musik Note für Note nachspielen oder kopieren könnte. Das wird niemals geschehen. Ruhe in Frieden, James Marshall Hendrix; du warst ein unglaublich begabter Mann.« 1970 drückte man das anders aus. Tony Palmer in electric revolution. Die Inside-Story der Pop-Stars1: »Jimi Hendrix spielte seine 240 V Gitarre mit den Zähnen, auf dem Rücken oder unterm Bein. Je nach Laune zertöpperte er sie oder steckte sie in Brand.« Geradezu ikonographischer Moment in der Geschichte des Rock als Pop: die weiße Strat in Flammen und daraufhin Anlass für Besucher und Glotzer, nach Monterey-Fanal nur darauf zu warten: wann spielt er die Saiten mit der Zunge, wann zerkloppt er die Klampfe, oder darf man erleben, dass er sie anzündet? Eine Nummernrevue, die vom Eigentlichen ablenkte. Frust.  Trotzdem, jetzt mal kurz: Die Finger verbrannte er sich im London Astoria (31. März 1967), in Monterey verfeuerte er »Wild Thing« (18. Juni 1967), bei Frank Zappa landeten irgendwann die Überreste einer beim Miami Pop Festival entflammten Stratocaster (19. Mai 1968).  Aber das Ding war, er war so ein krasser Gitarrist, dass… dass das allein schon genug war. Echt genug. Und der Showkram lenkte davon ab. Lou Reed »Er spielte ja rund um die Uhr«, erinnert Lou Reed, dessen Karriere mit Velvet Underground – selbe Zeit, selber Ort Greenwich Village – via Andy Warhol einen Schub bekam. »Seine Musik fand ich unterhaltsam, ebenso seine Show. Aber das Ding war, er war so ein krasser Gitarrist, dass… dass das allein schon genug war. Echt genug. Und der Showkram lenkte davon ab. Ich denke, das wurde ihm auch klar, und er wollte davon weg. Damit die Leute einfach auf die Musik achten. Unendlich viel hätte er noch bringen können. Aber die Situation, in der er eingeklemmt war… durch… entweder seine Plattenfirma, das Management, Konzertpromoter, die Publicity-Leute, dieser ganze Haufen Leute, mit denen man da zu tun hat. Die alle sagen ›Hey Jimi, wir haben doch diese Tour und du musst da, dort, da und dort und dort auch noch sein, so und so viele Leute kommen nicht rein, du solltest besser dies und das tun, dein Kontostand rutscht runter auf X, du willst Electric Ladyland [Studio] aufbauen und betreiben… vielleicht haut das nicht hin. Da lastete viel Druck auf ihm.«  Noch lange nicht ausgebrannt Was bleibt, sind die vier Jahre. Dazwischen Entfernungen und Grenzen und Stress, bei dem man schnell nicht mehr mitkriegt, wo oder warum man aufwacht. Is it tomorrow, or just the end of time? Und es bleiben drei offiziell abgenickte Studioalben. Mit rückwärts laufenden Tonbändern, Cartoon-ähnlichen Intros; und mit, generell ziemlich wenig beachtet: wahnsinnig berührenden Lyrics. Der essenzielle Punkt: Synästhesie, Comics oder Science-Fiction-Romane transferiert in Musik. Stimmungen. Lila Nebel als Gemütszustand, aber dabei eine hörbare Haltung. Das Ende war unnötig. Er hatte Pläne mit Miles Davis, liebelte mit Händel, Bach und dem ›Marsch‹ aus Tschaikowskis Nussknacker. Wollte sich in seinem Studio Electric Ladyland – wie die Beatles nach 1966 – nur noch dem Aufnehmen widmen. Da war noch so viel, da blieb noch so viel, was man mal machen müsste. Stattdessen wurden einige, nach seinem Tod und ohne sein Protestieren, sehr reich. In den ersten Nachrufen starb er mit 24. Andere spekulierten, er müsse ausgebrannt gewesen sein, nach so viel Drogen, so viel Exzess und Erfolg und Frauen und schlaflosen Nächten. John Mayall intonierte den Tod als unbeabsichtigte Überdosis2. Kleben blieb das Verdikt »nach neun Schlaftabletten an Erbrochenem erstickt … durch Selbstmord oder einen Unglücksfall« (Der Spiegel 31/1974). Das Nachspiel war ziemlich grässlich. Irre sponnen abartige Theorien.  Eric Burdon, der noch am 17. September mit Hendrix bei Ronnie Scott‘s Jazz Club jammte: »Er wirkte immer wie ein Geist, so gespenster-mäßig, er ließ niemanden an sich heran. Das Leben berührte er nur – das war sein Geheimnis –, an sich gerissen hat er nie irgendwas oder irgendwen.«   1 Tony Palmer: electric revolution. Die Inside Story der Pop-Stars, aus dem Englischen von Klaus Budzinski. Verlag Bärmeier & Nikel, Frankfurt/Main.2 »Accidental Suicide« auf John Mayall: Back to The Roots, Polydor 1971.

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑围绕1819年曼彻斯特圣彼得广场屠杀事件展开，由Young 'Uns成员Sean Cooney创作，邀请Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter等多位英国民谣歌手和乐手参与，以原创歌曲重现这一英国工人阶级历史中的标志性事件。专辑以书籍形式呈现，配以同时代的信件、政治漫画和插图，将历史叙事与音乐结合。歌曲捕捉了集会当日的期待与激动、军队冲入后转向恐惧与奔逃、以及事后的悲恸余波，聚焦于Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes等普通人的故事。乐评认为作品情感真挚、旋律有力，历史细节留于书中，而音乐本身具有长久的共鸣力。作为传统英国民谣历史题材作品，其风格偏向主流民谣叙事，与用户偏好的实验、前卫、电子或爵士方向距离较远。
